An Hạ10/11/2026 10:40 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!Sau vòng bình chọn cấp quốc gia với hơn 13 triệu lượt bình chọn, 11 nhà sáng tạo nội dung được chọn đại diện Việt Nam tham gia TikTok Awards Đông Nam Á 2026, tổ chức tại Bali, Indonesia vào cuối tháng 11.
Tối 9.11,TikToktổ chức họp báo công bố 11nhà sáng tạo nội dungđại diện Việt Nam tham dự TikTok Awards Đông Nam Á 2026. Đây là những gương mặt có lượt bình chọn cao nhất trong các hạng mục đề cử tại Việt Nam, sau giai đoạn bình chọn công khai từ ngày 12 - 26.10.2026. Những đại diện được lựa chọn sẽ tiếp tục tham gia vòng đánh giá cấp khu vực, cùng các nhà sáng tạo đến từ Indonesia, Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore và Thái Lan.
Danh sách 11 đại diện Việt Nam quy tụ nhiều gương mặt hoạt động trong các lĩnh vực khác nhau như giải trí, giáo dục, thể thao, ẩm thực, làm đẹp và lối sống.
Trần Hoàng Long, được biết đến với tênLong Chun, ghi dấu ấn qua những video hài hước, nội dung đời thường và hoạt động kinh doanh trên TikTok

Đỗ Kim Phúc là vận động viên bóng đá nghệ thuật, đồng thời thực hiện nhiều dự án thiện nguyện hướng đến trẻ em có hoàn cảnh khó khăn
Đỗ Ngọc Tường Minh chủ kênh Vitamin mèo, cô là người đứng sau giọng lồng tiếng hài hước, duyên dáng và chăm sóc dàn "boss" nổi tiếng trên mạng xã hội, đặc biệt là "chị" mèo Mỹ Diệu

Lê Nhựt Quan gây chú ý với kênh Quan Không Gờ, khai thác nét văn hóa Việt Nam qua các vùng quê và chợ địa phương
Trần Bảo Trân xây dựng nhân vật Rắn xà nẹo với phong cách bình luận hài hước, thẳng thắn về các hiện tượng mạng và chương trình truyền hình
Bùi Anh Ninh đại diện Việt Nam ở hạng mục Creator of the year. Anh là một trong những nhà sáng tạo nội dung được bình chọn nhiều tại Việt Nam
Trần Thị Thu Thủy chia sẻ những nội dung về chăm sóc da, trang điểm, thời trang và hành trình cải thiện bản thân
Nguyễn Thị Phương Thảo, được biết đến với tên Aley Nguyễn, là nhà sáng tạo nội dung livestream với nhiều thành tích tại các giải đấu TikTok live
Chia sẻ tại sự kiện,Long Chuncho biết: "Tôi muốn gửi lời cảm ơn đến ê kíp cùng cộng đồng khán giả, những người đã luôn ủng hộ để tôi đạt được thành tựu này. TikTok đã mở ra cơ hội để tôi tự do chia sẻ, kết nối và lan tỏa những câu chuyện tích cực, truyền cảm hứng đến cộng đồng. Trở thành một trong những đại diện Việt Nam tạiTikTok Awards Đông Nam Á2026 vừa là niềm tự hào, vừa là động lực để tôi phát triển hơn".
Phát biểu tại họp báo, ông Angga Anugrah Putra, Giám đốc Vận hành nội dung TikTok Đông Nam Á, gửi lời chúc mừng 11 nhà sáng tạo nội dung Việt Nam được bình chọn trở thành đại diện quốc gia. Theo ông, với thông điệp "The Ones Who Spark It" (Người thắp sáng cảm hứng), các nhà sáng tạo không chỉ phản ánh đời sống cộng đồng địa phương mà còn có thể biến đam mê thành động lực phát triển kinh tế và tạo ra những tác động xã hội tích cực.
Tại sự kiện, ông Nguyễn Ngọc Hồi, Phó giám đốc Sở Văn hóa và Thể thao TP.HCM, cũng nhấn mạnh vai trò của nội dung số trong đời sống xã hội. Ông cho rằng khi được tạo ra với tinh thần trách nhiệm và mục đích rõ ràng,nội dung sốcó thể góp phần thúc đẩy tiến bộ xã hội, cải thiện đời sống và tạo động lực phát triển kinh tế. Các nhà sáng tạo không chỉ thúc đẩy kinh tế sáng tạo mà còn có khả năng truyền cảm hứng đổi mới, khởi nghiệp cho thế hệ trẻ.
Các đại diện đến từ 6 quốc gia sẽ được đánh giá bởi hội đồng chuyên gia gồm đại diện Ban Thư ký ASEAN, Tập đoàn WPP và TikTok. Những gương mặt chiến thắng ở các hạng mục giải thưởng, cùng các đại diện được vinh danh tại ba hạng mục đặc biệt của từng quốc gia, sẽ được công bố trong đêm trao giải TikTok Awards Đông Nam Á 2026, diễn ra ngày 27.11 tại Bali, Indonesia.
Cựu tuyển thủ Ánh Viên, Võ Tấn Phát tranh suất đại diện Việt Nam tại TikTok Awards Đông Nam Á
TikTok Awards Đông Nam Á 2026 lần đầu được tổ chức với sự tham gia của 6 quốc gia. Tại Việt Nam, Ánh Viên, Võ Tấn Phát cùng Đặng Thu Hà, Ciin, Ngô Đức Duy góp mặt trong danh sách đề cử ở 11 hạng mục.Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.

fact_units.text: U23 Việt Nam - U23 Thái Lan (19h hôm nay): Thế hệ mới ra mắt | Báo Dân trí
U23 Việt Nam - U23 Thái Lan (19h hôm nay): Thế hệ mới ra mắt
(Dân trí) - Cả U23 Việt Nam và U23 Thái Lan đều trong quá trình chuẩn bị cho SEA Games 34 năm 2027 và giải U23 châu Á 2028, nên giải đấu ở Gia Lai có ý nghĩa quan trọng với cả hai đội tuyển.
*Trận đấu giữa đội tuyển U23 Việt Nam và U23 Thái Lan sẽ diễn ra lúc 19h tối nay (10/11), trên sân Pleiku (Gia Lai).
Dân trí sẽ tường thuật trực tuyến trận đấu này.
U23 Việt Nam dự giải U23 quốc tế ở Gia Lai mà không có một loạt cầu thủ từng làm nên thành công cho đội bóng này trong những năm gần đây.
U23 Việt Nam và U23 Thái Lan gần như làm mới lực lượng (Ảnh: VFF).

Những người đã chia tay đội tuyển U23 Việt Nam có thủ môn Trung Kiên, hậu vệ phải Minh Phúc, hậu vệ trái Khuất Văn Khang, trung vệ Hiểu Minh, Lý Đức, Nhật Minh, tiền vệ Xuân Bắc, Quốc Cường, tiền đạo Đình Bắc, Thanh Nhàn, Ngọc Mỹ, Quốc Việt.
Họ là những người từng vô địch giải U23 Đông Nam Á 2025, SEA Games 33 năm 2025, giành hạng ba giảiU23 châu Á2026.
Nhưng hiện tại những cầu thủ này đã quá tuổi dự SEA Games 34 năm 2027 và giải U23 châu Á 2028.
Theo quy định củaSEA Games34 và giải U23 châu Á 2028, các cầu thủ đủ điều kiện tham dự các giải đấu vừa nêu phải sinh năm 2005 trở về sau (năm nay 21 tuổi).
Chính vì thế, đội tuyển U23 Việt Nam dự giải U23 quốc tế ở Gia Lai thực chất là đội U21.
Thay thế cho thủ môn Trung Kiên là thủ môn Cao Văn Bình, thay thế cho các trung vệ Hiểu Minh, Nhật Minh, Lý Đức là các trung vệ Quang Kiệt, Mạnh Hưng, Nguyên Hoàng.
Williams Minh Hoàng là nhân tố mới của đội tuyển U23 Việt Nam (Ảnh: VFF).
Những nhân tố mới được chờ đợi ở hàng tiền vệ là Lê Văn Thuận, Thái Bá Đạt, Lê Đình Long Vũ.
Còn trên hàng tiền đạo, những cái tên như Williams Minh Hoàng, Trần Gia Bảo, Nguyễn Minh Tâm được kỳ vọng sẽ thay thế cho Đình Bắc, Thanh Nhàn, Quốc Việt.
Đội tuyển U23 Thái Lan cũng có thay đổi lớn.
Trung vệ Oussama Thiangkham, Chanapach Buaphan, Pichitchai Sienkrathok, tiền vệ Sittha Boonlha, Chawanwit Saelao, Kakana Khamyok, Seksan Ratree không còn khoác áo đội bóng trẻ xứ sở chùa vàng.
Những cầu thủ này cũng đã quá tuổi 21.
Điều đó có nghĩa là U23 Thái Lan và U23 Việt Nam sẽ đối đầu với nhau bằng những nhân sự rất khác, so với lần đối đầu gần nhất của hai đội ở trận chung kết SEA Games 33.
Với lợi thế sân nhà cùng dàn cầu thủ đang khát khao thể hiện năng lực, U23 Việt Nam được đánh giá cao hơn U23 Thái Lan trong trận đấu sắp diễn ra.
Điều quan trọng với các cầu thủ trẻ chủ nhà, đó là chúng ta sẽ tận dụng các cơ hội như thế nào?
Nếu các chân sút Williams Minh Hoàng và Trần Gia Bảo thể hiện được sự sắc bén, U23 Việt Nam đủ sức đánh bại U23 Thái Lan trên sân Pleiku.
HLV U23 Việt Nam tuyên bố về mục tiêu lớn khi đối đầu Thái Lan, Qatar
Theo HLV Đinh Hồng Vinh, giải giao hữu quốc tế tại Gia Lai 2026 là dịp để U23 Việt Nam tích lũy kinh nghiệm, chuẩn bị cho các mục tiêu tương lai, đặc biệt là những giải đấu quan trọng năm 2027.
HLV U23 Thái Lan quyết tâm đánh bại U23 Việt Nam, vươn tầm châu Á
Trước trận đấu với đội tuyển U23 Việt Nam vào tối mai (10/11), HLV Thawatchai Dumrongongtrakun của U23 Thái Lan cho biết đội bóng trẻ xứ sở chùa vàng quyết tâm vươn lên tầm châu Á.
U23 Việt Nam bất ngờ chia tay cầu thủ Việt kiều trước trận gặp Thái Lan
Hai cầu thủ Trần Thành Trung (CLB Ninh Bình) và Nguyễn Trọng Tuấn (CLB Hưng Yên) không thể góp mặt ở trận gặp U23 Thái Lan.
HLV Đinh Hồng Vinh đã triệu tập gấp người thay thế.
Các cầu thủ Việt kiều được kỳ vọng tỏa sáng ở U23 Việt Nam
Các cầu thủ Việt kiều Williams Minh Hoàng, Ngô Đăng Khoa và Trần Thành Trung nhận được nhiều kỳ vọng trong màu áo U23 Việt Nam tại giải U23 quốc tế 2026 ở Gia Lai.

Vừa giành Quả bóng vàng, Harry Kane đã nhận cú sốc lớn
(Dân trí) - Harry Kane bất ngờ bị loại khỏi Đội hình hay nhất thế giới FIFPro 2026, chỉ hai tuần sau khi ngôi sao người Anh giành Quả bóng vàng.
Ngôi sao của Bayern Munich đã có chiến thắng lịch sử vào tháng 10 khi trở thành cầu thủ người Anh đầu tiên giành Quả bóng vàng sau 25 năm. Trước đó, Michael Owen là người gần nhất củabóng đáAnh nhận danh hiệu cao quý này vào năm 2001.
Tuy nhiên, chỉ hai tuần sau khi được vinh danh là cầu thủ xuất sắc nhất thế giới, Harry Kane bất ngờ bị gạch tên khỏi Đội hình hay nhất thế giới FIFPro 2026 - giải thưởng do chính các cầu thủ chuyên nghiệp bình chọn dưới sự bảo trợ của FIFA.
Harry Kane chỉ xếp thứ 5 trong 8 tiền đạo được bình chọn vào đội hình hay nhất thế giới 2026, bất chấp anh vừa giành Quả bóng vàng FIFA hôm 26/10 (Ảnh: Getty).
Hơn 19.000 cầu thủ đến từ 73 quốc gia đã tham gia bình chọn Đội hình tiêu biểu nam và nữ năm nay. Tuy nhiên, Harry Kane không nhận đủ số phiếu để góp mặt trong đội hình danh giá này.
Tiền đạo chủ lực của đội tuyển Anh chỉ nhận được 27,6% số phiếu, qua đó bị loại khỏi danh sách 4 cầu thủ tấn công được lựa chọn vào đội hình hay nhấtthế giớinăm 2026.
Đội hình được bình chọn theo sơ đồ 3-3-4, với hàng công gồm Kylian Mbappe (46%), Lamine Yamal (37,4%), LionelMessi(29,5%) và Erling Haaland (28,4%). Đáng chú ý, Cristiano Ronaldo cũng không có tên trong đội hình chính thức. Dù lọt vào danh sách 8 tiền đạo được đề cử, siêu sao người Bồ Đào Nha chỉ nhận được 13,2% số phiếu, thấp nhất trong nhóm này.
Việc Kane bị loại đánh dấu lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử FIFPro có một cầu thủ giành Quả bóng vàng nhưng không góp mặt trong Đội hình hay nhất thế giới cùng năm. Giải thưởng Đội hình hay nhất năm được tổ chức lần đầu vào năm 2005. Vì vậy, trường hợp của Kane cũng là lần đầu tiên trong 21 năm xảy ra nghịch lý này.
Ở những vị trí còn lại, đội tuyển Anh vẫn có đại diện là Jude Bellingham. Tiền vệ của Real Madrid được lựa chọn ở hàng tiền vệ sau màn trình diễn ấn tượng tạiWorld Cuphồi tháng 7. Anh đá cặp cùng Rodri, đội trưởng đội tuyển Tây Ban Nha và Vitinha của Paris Saint-Germain.
Trong sơ đồ ba hậu vệ, trung vệ Pau Cubarsi của Barcelona được lựa chọn, cùng với Nuno Mendes và Achraf Hakimi ở hai hành lang cánh. Một bất ngờ khác xuất hiện ở vị trí thủ môn khi David Raya của Arsenal được lựa chọn thay vì người đồng đội ở đội tuyển Tây Ban Nha, Unai Simon.
Đội hình hay nhất thế giới FIFPro 2026 được bình chọn bởi hơn 19.000 cầu thủ đến từ 73 quốc gia.
Đội hình hay nhất thế giới năm nay chắc chắn sẽ gây tranh cãi, đặc biệt bởi sự vắng mặt của Kane. Tuy nhiên, tiền đạo người Anh không phải ngôi sao lớn duy nhất bị loại. Những cái tên đáng chú ý khác không góp mặt gồm chủ nhân Quả bóng vàng 2025 Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia và Michael Olise.
Trong khi đó, việc Messi được lựa chọn đánh dấu sự trở lại của siêu sao người Argentina trong Đội hình hay nhất năm kể từ năm 2023. Đây cũng là lần thứ 18 anh góp mặt trong đội hình danh giá này.
Tài năng trẻ người Tây Ban Nha Lamine Yamal cũng thiết lập cột mốc đáng chú ý khi lần thứ hai liên tiếp được lựa chọn vào Đội hình hay nhất năm, sau lần đầu tiên vào năm 2025. Ở tuổi 19, Yamal trở thành cầu thủ trẻ nhất hai lần góp mặt trong đội hình này. Thành tích đó phần nào giúp anh vơi đi nỗi thất vọng khi không giành được Quả bóng vàng.
Harry Kane được xướng tên ở vị trí cao nhất tại lễ trao giải Quả bóng vàng (Ballon d’Or 2026) ở London, qua đó lần đầu tiên trong sự nghiệp sở hữu danh hiệu cá nhân danh giá nhất bóng đá thế giới.
Harry Kane nhận cú hích lớn sau khi giành Quả bóng vàng 2026
Harry Kane đã trở thành cầu thủ được trả lương cao nhất châu Âu, chỉ hơn một tuần sau khi giành Quả bóng vàng 2026.
Biểu cảm của Yamal và Mbappe khi Harry Kane giành Quả bóng vàng 2026
Hai cầu thủ Lamine Yamal và Kylian Mbappe đã có phản ứng trái ngược sau khi Harry Kane giành giải Quả bóng vàng 2026.
Quả bóng vàng 2026 bị tố dàn xếp để Harry Kane giành danh hiệu
Nhiều nguồn tin trên thế giới đã nghi ngờ Ban tổ chức giải Quả bóng vàng 2026 dàn xếp để Harry Kane giành danh hiệu.

Khởi tranh Giải bóng bàn Cây Vợt Vàng sau 7 năm vắng bóng
Tối 5-11, Giải bóng bàn Cây Vợt Vàng lần thứ 34 chính thức bước vào tranh tài, đánh dấu sự hồi sinh của một sân chơi huyền thoại.
Giải bóng bàn Cây Vợt Vàng trở lại với sau 7 năm vắng bóng - Ảnh: ĐỨC KHUÊ
Lễ khai mạc Giảibóng bànCây Vợt Vàng lần thứ 34 diễn ra vào tối 5-11 tại Nhà thi đấu Hồ Xuân Hương (P. Xuân Hòa, TP.HCM). Sau 7 năm gián đoạn, giải đấu lâu đời này mới chính thức trở lại.
Sự trở lại của giải không chỉ đáp ứng mong đợi của người hâm mộ mà còn khẳng định nỗ lực của ngành thể thao TP.HCM trong việc duy trì và phát triển một sân chơi quốc tế uy tín.
Tuyển bóng bàn Việt Nam được treo thưởng khủng trước giải Đông Nam Á
Giải đấu diễn ra từ ngày 5 đến 8-11, quy tụ hơn 121 vận động viên thuộc 19 đội nam và 11 đội nữ, đến từ: Nhật Bản, Singapore, Đài Bắc Trung Hoa, Hồng Kông (Trung Quốc), Lào và Việt Nam. Các tay vợt thi đấu ở 4 nội dung gồm: đồng đội nam, đồng đội nữ, đơn nam và đơn nữ.
Đáng chú ý, Nhật Bản đem sang 2 CLB thuộc nhóm mạnh trong nước là Ishida TTC và Shotoku. Trong khi đó, CLB TTF đến từ Lào quy tụ dàn VĐV chất lượng đến từ Thụy Điển.
Dù vậy, các đội của nước chủ nhà lại không thể cử được những tay vợt xuất sắc nhất, do đội tuyển đang chuẩn bị cho Giải bóng bàn vô địch Đông Nam Á.
Các tay vợt tham dự lễ khai mạc tối 5-11 - Ảnh: ĐỨC KHUÊ
Tuy nhiên, người hâm mộ vẫn có cơ hội chứng kiến những gương mặt triển vọng của bóng bàn Việt Nam như: Nguyễn Bạch Thanh Thư, Nguyễn Thị Xuân Mai, Bùi Hữu Huy, Nguyễn Hoàng Lâm...
Phát biểu tại lễ khai mạc, ông Mai Bá Hùng, Chủ tịch Liên đoàn bóng bàn TP.HCM, cho biết: Cây Vợt Vàng là giải đấu quốc tế có uy tín và bề dày lịch sử hàng đầu của bóng bàn Việt Nam suốt hơn 3 thập kỷ qua.
Sự trở lại của giải được kỳ vọng sẽ tiếp tục tạo động lực phát triển phong trào bóng bàn trong nước, đồng thời nâng cao năng lực vận động viên trên đấu trường quốc tế.
'Lão bà' 43 tuổi thắng sốc siêu sao bóng bàn Trung Quốc
Dù đã 43 tuổi và từng hai lần đứt gân Achilles, tay vợt Han Ying vẫn khiến bóng bàn Trung Quốc phải e ngại khi liên tiếp đánh bại những ngôi sao hàng đầu thế giới.

fact_units.text: Vừa giành Quả bóng vàng, Harry Kane đã nhận cú sốc lớn | Báo Dân trí
Vừa giành Quả bóng vàng, Harry Kane đã nhận cú sốc lớn
(Dân trí) - Harry Kane bất ngờ bị loại khỏi Đội hình hay nhất thế giới FIFPro 2026, chỉ hai tuần sau khi ngôi sao người Anh giành Quả bóng vàng.
Ngôi sao của Bayern Munich đã có chiến thắng lịch sử vào tháng 10 khi trở thành cầu thủ người Anh đầu tiên giành Quả bóng vàng sau 25 năm.
Trước đó, Michael Owen là người gần nhất củabóng đáAnh nhận danh hiệu cao quý này vào năm 2001.

Tuy nhiên, chỉ hai tuần sau khi được vinh danh là cầu thủ xuất sắc nhất thế giới, Harry Kane bất ngờ bị gạch tên khỏi Đội hình hay nhất thế giới FIFPro 2026 - giải thưởng do chính các cầu thủ chuyên nghiệp bình chọn dưới sự bảo trợ của FIFA.
Harry Kane chỉ xếp thứ 5 trong 8 tiền đạo được bình chọn vào đội hình hay nhất thế giới 2026, bất chấp anh vừa giành Quả bóng vàng FIFA hôm 26/10 (Ảnh: Getty).
Hơn 19.000 cầu thủ đến từ 73 quốc gia đã tham gia bình chọn Đội hình tiêu biểu nam và nữ năm nay.
Tuy nhiên, Harry Kane không nhận đủ số phiếu để góp mặt trong đội hình danh giá này.
Tiền đạo chủ lực của đội tuyển Anh chỉ nhận được 27,6% số phiếu, qua đó bị loại khỏi danh sách 4 cầu thủ tấn công được lựa chọn vào đội hình hay nhấtthế giớinăm 2026.
Đội hình được bình chọn theo sơ đồ 3-3-4, với hàng công gồm Kylian Mbappe (46%), Lamine Yamal (37,4%), LionelMessi(29,5%) và Erling Haaland (28,4%).
Đáng chú ý, Cristiano Ronaldo cũng không có tên trong đội hình chính thức.
Dù lọt vào danh sách 8 tiền đạo được đề cử, siêu sao người Bồ Đào Nha chỉ nhận được 13,2% số phiếu, thấp nhất trong nhóm này.
Việc Kane bị loại đánh dấu lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử FIFPro có một cầu thủ giành Quả bóng vàng nhưng không góp mặt trong Đội hình hay nhất thế giới cùng năm.
Giải thưởng Đội hình hay nhất năm được tổ chức lần đầu vào năm 2005.
Vì vậy, trường hợp của Kane cũng là lần đầu tiên trong 21 năm xảy ra nghịch lý này.
Ở những vị trí còn lại, đội tuyển Anh vẫn có đại diện là Jude Bellingham.
Tiền vệ của Real Madrid được lựa chọn ở hàng tiền vệ sau màn trình diễn ấn tượng tạiWorld Cuphồi tháng 7.
Anh đá cặp cùng Rodri, đội trưởng đội tuyển Tây Ban Nha và Vitinha của Paris Saint-Germain.
Trong sơ đồ ba hậu vệ, trung vệ Pau Cubarsi của Barcelona được lựa chọn, cùng với Nuno Mendes và Achraf Hakimi ở hai hành lang cánh.
Một bất ngờ khác xuất hiện ở vị trí thủ môn khi David Raya của Arsenal được lựa chọn thay vì người đồng đội ở đội tuyển Tây Ban Nha, Unai Simon.
Đội hình hay nhất thế giới FIFPro 2026 được bình chọn bởi hơn 19.000 cầu thủ đến từ 73 quốc gia.
Đội hình hay nhất thế giới năm nay chắc chắn sẽ gây tranh cãi, đặc biệt bởi sự vắng mặt của Kane.
Tuy nhiên, tiền đạo người Anh không phải ngôi sao lớn duy nhất bị loại.
Những cái tên đáng chú ý khác không góp mặt gồm chủ nhân Quả bóng vàng 2025 Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia và Michael Olise.
Trong khi đó, việc Messi được lựa chọn đánh dấu sự trở lại của siêu sao người Argentina trong Đội hình hay nhất năm kể từ năm 2023.
Đây cũng là lần thứ 18 anh góp mặt trong đội hình danh giá này.
Tài năng trẻ người Tây Ban Nha Lamine Yamal cũng thiết lập cột mốc đáng chú ý khi lần thứ hai liên tiếp được lựa chọn vào Đội hình hay nhất năm, sau lần đầu tiên vào năm 2025.
Ở tuổi 19, Yamal trở thành cầu thủ trẻ nhất hai lần góp mặt trong đội hình này.
Thành tích đó phần nào giúp anh vơi đi nỗi thất vọng khi không giành được Quả bóng vàng.
Harry Kane được xướng tên ở vị trí cao nhất tại lễ trao giải Quả bóng vàng (Ballon d’Or 2026) ở London, qua đó lần đầu tiên trong sự nghiệp sở hữu danh hiệu cá nhân danh giá nhất bóng đá thế giới.
Harry Kane nhận cú hích lớn sau khi giành Quả bóng vàng 2026
Harry Kane đã trở thành cầu thủ được trả lương cao nhất châu Âu, chỉ hơn một tuần sau khi giành Quả bóng vàng 2026.
Biểu cảm của Yamal và Mbappe khi Harry Kane giành Quả bóng vàng 2026
Hai cầu thủ Lamine Yamal và Kylian Mbappe đã có phản ứng trái ngược sau khi Harry Kane giành giải Quả bóng vàng 2026.
Quả bóng vàng 2026 bị tố dàn xếp để Harry Kane giành danh hiệu
Nhiều nguồn tin trên thế giới đã nghi ngờ Ban tổ chức giải Quả bóng vàng 2026 dàn xếp để Harry Kane giành danh hiệu.

Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today.
Image: Cath Virginia / The VergeJay Peters
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.
Anthropicis announcingtwo new models today: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says are designed to take on “daunting” technical challenges. The company claims the new models show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, and can generate outputs faster than the 5.1 versions of the Fable and Mythos models.
Claude Fable 5.2 is good at challenging software engineering problems, Anthropic says, and can orchestrate agent teams and tackle long-running projects. The new model has also solved some complex scientific problems, including two open theoretical physics problems.
During prerelease testing, the two models have “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours,” Anthropic says.
Claude Fable 5.2 is launching today. As for Claude Mythos 5.2, only vetted organizations will have access to start. The new 5.2 models follow the release of Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1in September.

Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 ahead of IPOSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
Anthropic released two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2.
The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released frontier models since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow down the pace of AI development.
Anthropic is gearing up for what is expected to be a blockbuster IPO.
Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during an interview at Anthropic's headquarters in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, April 30, 2026.Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty Images
Anthropicon Monday released two newartificial intelligencemodels, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as the company readies for apotentially historic IPOthat could take place as soon as next week.
Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are Anthropic's most advanced offerings, and the company said they generate outputs 30% faster than their predecessors. The models also cost 20% less than the 5.1 generation, and will be available for $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, the company said.
The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released so-called "frontier" models since its CEO,Dario Amodei, called toslow downthe pace of AI developmentin September. Anthropic said the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release.
"We called for pacing, not pausing," Dianne Penn, Anthropic's head of product management for research, told CNBC in an interview.
Anthropic has to balance its safety efforts with intense commercial and competitive pressures, a tension that the company highlighted in theextensive risk factors sectionof itsprospectuslate last month. And as executives prepare to kick off Anthropic'sIPO roadshow, they'll have to convince investors that their approach is the right one.
The company is aiming for a valuation of $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion in its offering, as CNBCpreviously reported, down from a target of $2 trillion that had been floated in recent months.

Anthropic firstintroduced Mythosin April, and it limited the rollout to a select group of organizations because of the model's advanced cybersecurity capabilities. The companyintroduced Fable, a publicly available version of Mythos with additional safeguards, two months later.
The models — particularly Mythos — captivatedWall Streetandgovernment officialsalike, and they helped to fuel Anthropic's meteoric rise this year. The company said in itsamended prospectusthat it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year.
Penn said Fable 5.2 is primarily intended for "power users or power use cases" since it excels at complex, open-ended technical work. Other models likeClaude Opus 5.5, which Anthropic released in September, are better suited for daily tasks, so Penn said users should turn to Fable 5.2 when they need to tackle hard problems in engineering, mathematics and robotics.
"These are just net new things that are completely novel, and so they're frontier use cases," Penn said. "We expect that over time to maybe trickle to the Opus class, but really right now we do see a difference in terms of performance that we think those frontier use cases benefit from."
Anthropic said Fable 5.2 is generally available on Monday, and Mythos 5.2 is available to vetted organizations through the company's Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.

Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
Russell Brandom2:41 PM PST · November 3, 2026
Anthropic is working on an open source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system,called FlashProve, is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” — a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using.
Similar tocryptographic email signaturesthat let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results.
FlashProve could also be used to verify claims by third parties that a specific task was done by an advanced model. “A developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model,” the researchers write. “How can a user verify these claims?”
To work, the system requires AI labs to publish a “fingerprint” of each model they release that can later be matched to specific outputs and verified cryptographically. Crucially, the fingerprints don’t reveal a model’s weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves and which closed-model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI keep private. That means labs could publish the fingerprints without giving up their most valuable asset, enabling the system to work with commercial models, too. The system is also designed to be lightweight, so verification could be performed on a local device.
As part of the announcement, researchers releaseda detailed technical specificationand working code for various elements of the system, which is publicly availableunder an open source license on GitHub. Research in the system is ongoing, and there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab.
“This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda,” researchers explain in the announcement post. “We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.”

Anthropic released two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2.
The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released frontier models since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow down the pace of AI development.
Anthropic is gearing up for what is expected to be a blockbuster IPO.

Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during an interview at Anthropic's headquarters in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, April 30, 2026.Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty Images

Anthropicon Monday released two newartificial intelligencemodels, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as the company readies for apotentially historic IPOthat could take place as soon as next week.
Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are Anthropic's most advanced offerings, and the company said they generate outputs 30% faster than their predecessors.
The models also cost 20% less than the 5.1 generation, and will be available for $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, the company said.
The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released so-called "frontier" models since its CEO,Dario Amodei, called toslow downthe pace of AI developmentin September.
Anthropic said the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release.
"We called for pacing, not pausing," Dianne Penn, Anthropic's head of product management for research, told CNBC in an interview.

Anthropic has to balance its safety efforts with intense commercial and competitive pressures, a tension that the company highlighted in theextensive risk factors sectionof itsprospectuslate last month.
And as executives prepare to kick off Anthropic'sIPO roadshow, they'll have to convince investors that their approach is the right one.
The company is aiming for a valuation of $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion in its offering, as CNBCpreviously reported, down from a target of $2 trillion that had been floated in recent months.

Ben White made his first England appearance in more than three years against Uruguay in March
Arsenal defender Ben White says people do not know the "full story" behind his decision to previously make himself unavailable for England selection - but says he would make the same decision again.
White, who has beennamed in Thomas Tuchel's squadfor upcoming Nations League fixtures,left the Three Lions' campat the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons.
He thenmade himself unavailablefor selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate's reign, andwas booed by some fansin March's 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Tuchel.
Asked by BBC Radio 5 live's football correspondent John Murray what he would say to people who define his England career by what happened in Qatar, White said: "I think obviously people don't know the full story, because I [have] never said anything and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that.
"I think that is probably the best way.
"It's been amazing [though], obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it is amazing to be here now."
White is now 29 and asked if he would have done anything differently in hindsight, he added: "No, I don't think I would.
"Obviously, I was a bit younger, I am a bit older now.
"I think as a person I am quite real and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make.
"So, one that I am not happy about, but obviously it happened and [it is] time to move on."
White came on for his first England appearance since 2022 in March's 1-1 draw with Uruguay and was booed by some supporters before he scored but also gave away the penalty that led to the visitors' equaliser.
After that, Chelsea midfielder Jordan Henderson said he and his fellow England playerswould always supportWhite, while Tuchelsaid recentlythat the defender deserves "a new chapter" and "positive feedback from the crowd".
Asked how he dealt with the emotions of that night at Wembley, White added: "Before the game I was thinking 'don't not stand out, but [take it] nice and easy'.
"Then I came on and obviously got booed, then I scored, then I gave away a penalty.
"So, it was obviously full of emotions that night, [but] it was a good night."
England play Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before taking on world champions Spain in Madrid three days later.
White is looking to add to his six England caps in this international break and said: It is obviously an amazing privilege to be called up.
"The feeling is the same every time you do get this chance to play for England. It's one I am really looking forward to this week."

Chernobyl’s Dogs May Be Evolving, but Scientists Don’t Know Why | WIREDSkip to main content
The dogs livingnear thedisaster siteof the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant are not like other dogs—at least as far as their genomes go. In recent years, researchers uncovered a unique genetic profile among this population, but what’s driven this distinction remained unclear.
The explanation that’s perhaps most tantalizing to asci-fi authoris that the persistent radiation at thenuclear sitehas caused mutations to accumulate in the dogs’ genomes. But there are other ways a population’s genetics can change over time, such as random drift or natural selection. A recent study published in the scientific journalGenesrevisited these pups, searching for genetic patterns pointing to one of these processes.
The researchers compared the DNA from dogs living in the area right around the nuclear plant with genetic material from dogs living in thecity of Chernobyl, about 16 kilometers away. They also compared these canines to other global dog populations. The contrast alone was extreme. The dogs in Chernobyl city “are more genetically similar to dogs in theGalapagos Islandsthan they are to the dog population” at the nuclear plant, said Megan Dillon, a postdoctoral researcher at North Carolina State University and first author of the study.
But more striking still, the comparison revealed that random chance alone could not explain the differences between the dog populations. Instead, it seems the dogs at the nuclear site have been experiencing natural selection.
“When I was first doing those analyzes, I had to kind of pause and was like, ‘Wow, I have to make sure I'm doing all of this right,’ because this is very interesting, very surprising,” Dillon said.
A dog walks through the ghost town of Pripyat near Chernobyl's nuclear power plant.Photograph: SERGEI SUPINSKY/Getty Images
Not only did the dogs seem to be evolving, but some of the genomic regions under the highest selective pressure were associated with functions such as DNA repair, immunity, and cell survival. In other words, certain genetic differences in the dogs from the plant could be relevant for coping with environmental stress.
Instead of being mutations, these genomic variants likely already existed among local dogs but became more common in the population over the past 40 years. “These dog populations already had this high degree ofgenetic diversity,” Dillon said. “Maybe this founding population at the power plant had the kind ofgenetic toolkitto endure and survive in these harsh conditions. It’s not necessarily that they were being bombarded with new mutations.”
Taken together, the results support the hypothesis thatnatural selectioncontributed to the difference seen in the dogs at Chernobyl compared to other populations. What remains unclear is which environmental factors favored these variants and whether they provide any specific advantage. “Even though we found this evidence of selection and it is around these biologically relevant genes, we still cannot say that this is tied to the exposures that the dogs have faced,” Dillon noted.
Radiation at the disaster site might seem like the easiest explanation to point to, but there are many other selective pressures this dog population has faced sincenuclear meltdown. Chernobyl’s dogs are descended frompets left behindduring the evacuations. Since then, they’ve persisted through Ukraine’s harsh winters and weathered other pollutants including heavy metals and pesticides also deposited in the area. “A lot of these contaminants have similar signatures and similar pathology,” Dillon said. “There are just too many different things to really be able to tease apart a single variable.”
The researchers also don’t have access to longitudinal samples that would show exactly how this population has changed over time. “It's almost like looking at a single still image and trying to figure out what came before it,” said Matthew Breen, a professor of genomics at North Carolina State University and the study’s senior author. “Those first few years were probably the most critical period—if they were selected, that's when thatselection processwould have happened.”
It’s not possible to go back and get samples from the dogs who lived there in 1986, a time when no organism—not even a bacterium—had its full genome sequenced. Breen was a graduate student in England then. “I was involved in a project driving around the Welsh mountain hills, collecting sheep from the pastures because theradioactive cloudhad blown over Western Europe,” he recalled. There wasn’t anything to see in the data gathered then, but the technology has evolved, and those sheep had also not been living at the center of a nuclear meltdown for generations.
Nearly four decades after the accident, the Chernobyl exclusion zone has also become arefuge for wildlife. Wolves, deer, wild boars, and lynx now roam the area—a return that researchers largely attribute to the decline in human activity. Among some of these residents, such as the wolf population, researchers have also observed similar genomic distinctions to those seen in the dogs.
“It really demonstrates theresilience of natureto catastrophic events caused by humans,” Breen said. “You push something in one direction, it can respond to that and either push back or deviate its path going forward. I think this is what we're seeing here.”

England’s first-choice back three stares Borthwick in face after Australia rout | England rugby union team | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank excelled playing in England’s back three for the first time in two years against Australia.Photograph: Matt Impey/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenImmanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank excelled playing in England’s back three for the first time in two years against Australia.Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock
England’s first-choice back three stares Borthwick in face after Australia rout
Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank can make an impact at next year’s World Cup, providing they can all stay fit
Rugby, at its heart, is a simple game. Win the collisions and you’ll more than likely win the match. Rule the skies, own the floor and the chances are you’ll end up on the right side of the ledger. Put square pegs in square holes and you can achieve the sort of attacking fluidity required for a record score against Australia. The complicated bit, once you stop trying to put them in round holes, is keeping those square pegs fit.
England’s emphatic winover the Wallabies on Sunday was the first time in two years Borthwick has been able to field a back-three of Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank. It was also the first time ever that they have lined up with 11, 14 and 15 on their respective backs. It will not be the last but it was a fleeting glimpse nonetheless. Feyi-Waboso sustained an ankle injury that will rule him out for the rest of the autumn campaign. Furbank has a groin problem that will keep him sidelined against Japan and given Borthwick is considering resting some players, it may be Freeman sits out on Saturday. It could conceivably be an entirely different back three against Eddie Jones’s side.
Steve Borthwick’s England channel their rage to resemble finished article | Andy BullRead more
Given how serious it is, Feyi-Waboso’s ankle injury was the major blot on England’s copybook against Australia. His time on the field was both a reminder of how devastating a runner he can be and how susceptible to injury he is. Feyi-Waboso’s handling was not perfect but it took him about 90 seconds to showcase the threat he possesses when scoring his disallowed try, cruising through a gap prised open for him by Fin Smith.
In his 40 minutes on the pitch, Feyi-Waboso made 130 metres from his eight carries, demonstrating time and again how elusive he is. As Borthwick remarked after Sunday’s victory, the game favours attacking sides who can keep making ground and keep recycling the ball at present, and in Feyi-Waboso England have someone who will always ensure opposition defences are scrambling.
On the evidence of his showing against Australia and his previous outing with Argentina, it does not feel hyperbolic to say England become anentirely different propositionwith the 23-year-old winger in the side. England’s attack coach Lee Blackett knows all about Feyi-Waboso’s threats from their time together at Wasps and with Smith purring as he did on Sunday, the fly-half has the ability to unleash Borthwick’s most dangerous runner.
The trouble is, it has not happened often enough since Feyi-Waboso made his debut in early 2024. Now that he is out of the rest of England’s November Tests, he will have managed just 17 appearances in England’s 36 matches since and including his debut come the end of the year. A hamstring injury threatened his involvement this autumn, it was the same issue that forced him to miss the Six Nations and a shoulder problem that ruled him out of the Championship 12 months earlier. He has not managed to string together more than five consecutive starts for England in his career.
Furbank, meanwhile, made his first appearance for England on Sunday since the 2024 autumn victory over Japan. His run of bad luck with injuries has been astonishing – struck down by appendicitis when finally set to make his comeback over the summer – but the gracefulness with which he played against the Wallabies was a joy to watch. Wearing white boots to match his kit only added to the impression that Furbank glides across the pitch. His break to set up Jack van Poortvliet’s try was the champagne moment of an effervescent display, a reminder of what England have missed in his absence. The hope must be that he is fit to face the All Blacks on Saturday week.
View image in fullscreenSteve Borthwick has tried many combinations since Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank last lined up for England together.Photograph: Mark Chappell/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock
Freeman’s “second debut” for England came in the same match in which Feyi-Waboso won his first cap, having been overlooked for the first 12 months of Borthwick’s tenure. He went on to cement his status of one of the world’s leading wingers, before Borthwick preserved with attempting to reinvent him as an outside-centre. Given Freeman has started the past three matches back on the right wing, it seems common sense has won the day.
In the two years since they all last lined up together, England have tried all manner of combinations. Freddie Steward and Tom Roebuck enjoyed a degree of success when aerial supremacy was all the rage, but it does not feel like a coincidence that during England’s worst Six Nations campaign this year Feyi-Waboso was injured throughout, Furbank was overlooked and Freeman was often deployed at centre. For thefirst defeat by Italy, not one of them appeared in the back three.
With 11 months before England’s World Cup opener against Tonga, however, Borthwick has his first-choice back three combination now staring him in the face. The perfect blend of stylish playmaker at full-back, a robust, ultra-consistent performer on one wing, a game-breaker on the other.
England’s budget does not stretch to the amount of cotton wool required to ensure they all make the plane to Australia next year, but there are echoes of the 2019 contingent of Elliot Daly, Anthony Watson and Jonny May with the current trio. If victory over awoeful Wallabies sidetold us anything it is that England have a set of outside backs to make the rest of the world sit up and take note once more, provided they can all stay fit. The problem is it remains a big if.

Nations Championship: Matt Dawson column - England make massive step up in 45-22 win vs Australia - BBC Sport
In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on an impressive 45-22 win for Steve Borthwick's side against Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday.
Beating Australia with their record points tally against the Wallabies was a very positive way for England to start the autumn series, given the break they have had and how the beginning of the year went.
England were very accurate, very disciplined, creative and genuinely did not give Australia a sniff.
Before the game, I was expecting Australia to provide much more of a stern test. Some people might be a bit too critical of Australia, saying they did not turn up, but I think it edges more towards how well England played than how average Australia were.
I am not saying by any stretch that it was the perfect performance but, all in all, it was a massive step up from the Six Nations and even from the Nations Championship games in the summer.
Intensity, accuracy and discipline in abundance
Watch: England score seven tries in record-breaking win against Australia
A couple of days before the Australia game, Jamie George said the England teamhad been galvanisedby a newspaper article which claimed the end of their summer tour had been marked by player unrest over head coach Borthwick's leadership.
When you are inside those international camps, you are very deliberate in staying tight and not letting anybody in in whatever way, shape or form, therefore you become very sensitive to any kind of criticism.
There is a reason for doing that - it draws you together and allows you to create a bit more determination and drive to be successful.
You could see England's intensity, their accuracy and their discipline. All the things that have maybe been highlighted over the past nine months as things England have been lacking, there was an abundance of all of it.
As much as it is easy to try to pick holes in England because it is England, sometimes you have got to pat people on the back and say they got it right.
The opposition was dangerous with good individual players, but from the off England's tactics were spot on. Their decision-making was controlled and they looked like a very well-drilled side.
England swat aside Wallabies to back up Borthwick
Feyi-Waboso burns bright as England energy endorses Borthwick
How England might unlock the best of Slade
England's back three of George Furbank, Tommy Freeman and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso caused plenty of problems for Australia, but I think you have to include Fin Smith and Henry Slade in that as well.
Potentially, there is something in that backline that may allow us to see the Slade we see for Exeter that we have not seen as much for England.
Having the likes of Feyi-Waboso, Freeman and Furbank around Slade and them understanding the sorts of positions he can get them into - there might be some long-term benefits to that.
Feyi-Waboso is X-factor, there is no question about that. For his early disallowed try, he shifted his weight and beat someone with that pace - I do not think there are many people in the world who could do that.
When you have got players like him who can do that regularly, all of a sudden you are getting momentum.
There was a massive difference in ruck speed and in momentum; England were getting lined up defensively and pushing Australia back, whereas when you have got players like Feyi-Waboso and Ben Earl, and then when Henry Pollock comes on as well, you have got plenty of players who can break the line in traffic and it makes attacking that much easier.
Fin Smith is leading the team, he looks like he is a general and in control of the game.
He has got a safe pair of hands and communication from Seb Atkinson, he has got vision from Slade and then a back three that if you give them half a chance, they are going to bust the line, create opportunities and probably finish.
There were bits of Sunday's game where if New Zealand were doing it, everybody would be ranting and raving about how complete some of those tries were.
Pollock's flexibility a fantastic weapon
Image source,Press AssociationImage caption,
Henry Pollock has five tries in four Nations Championship matches, with only New Zealand's Will Jordan (six) scoring more
Feyi-Waboso's injury meant Pollock came off the bench to play in an unfamiliar position on the wing and he ended up scoring two of England's seven tries.
He did very well considering he was on for a whole half. Going forward, what is the difference having Pollock there? He has got a winger's speed, the step, great hands, the power and the bulk that other wingers do not have and he is going to be a handful for the opposition.
Defensively, he was tested a couple of times and that is inevitable, but to have that flexibility on the bench allows England to have that six-two split because you have got a player who can now pretty much cover so many positions.
As great as it was, and I am sure he absolutely loved it, unfortunately he is probably inking himself in to be quite a significant bench player moving forward, which is not really what I think he would like to be labelled as.
Selfishly, from an England point of view, it is a fantastic weapon to have.
The whole bench did really well and made a difference. It goes all the way back to selection, something Borthwick has previously come under fire for a little bit.
It does not mean that just because he has got one right, the autumn is going to go swimmingly well, but from the off the selection has been right, the gameplan was a bit more expansive than I thought it was going to be and they absolutely nailed the execution.
Will England back it up against Japan?
Tactically, I loved the balance of the England performance; a really dominant set-piece, driving mauls and in-your-face defence.
England have maybe always been like that but have lacked the discipline to go with it.
Against Australia, they proved they have the capability to be disciplined and maintain concentration - and I want to see that over the next three weeks.
Can they, under more pressure - because they are going to face more pressure, particularly against New Zealand - still maintain that discipline and decision-making?
They have got the assets to overpower Japan, but can they do it by giving away fewer than 10 penalties? Can they do it by having 15 people on the pitch for 80 minutes?

fact_units.text: England’s first-choice back three stares Borthwick in face after Australia rout | England rugby union team | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank excelled playing in England’s back three for the first time in two years against Australia.Photograph: Matt Impey/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenImmanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank excelled playing in England’s back three for the first time in two years against Australia.Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock
England’s first-choice back three stares Borthwick in face after Australia rout
Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank can make an impact at next year’s World Cup, providing they can all stay fit
Win the collisions and you’ll more than likely win the match.
Rule the skies, own the floor and the chances are you’ll end up on the right side of the ledger.
Put square pegs in square holes and you can achieve the sort of attacking fluidity required for a record score against Australia.
The complicated bit, once you stop trying to put them in round holes, is keeping those square pegs fit.
England’s emphatic winover the Wallabies on Sunday was the first time in two years Borthwick has been able to field a back-three of Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank.
It was also the first time ever that they have lined up with 11, 14 and 15 on their respective backs.
It will not be the last but it was a fleeting glimpse nonetheless.
Feyi-Waboso sustained an ankle injury that will rule him out for the rest of the autumn campaign.
Furbank has a groin problem that will keep him sidelined against Japan and given Borthwick is considering resting some players, it may be Freeman sits out on Saturday.
It could conceivably be an entirely different back three against Eddie Jones’s side.
Steve Borthwick’s England channel their rage to resemble finished article | Andy BullRead more
Given how serious it is, Feyi-Waboso’s ankle injury was the major blot on England’s copybook against Australia.
His time on the field was both a reminder of how devastating a runner he can be and how susceptible to injury he is.
Feyi-Waboso’s handling was not perfect but it took him about 90 seconds to showcase the threat he possesses when scoring his disallowed try, cruising through a gap prised open for him by Fin Smith.
In his 40 minutes on the pitch, Feyi-Waboso made 130 metres from his eight carries, demonstrating time and again how elusive he is.

As Borthwick remarked after Sunday’s victory, the game favours attacking sides who can keep making ground and keep recycling the ball at present, and in Feyi-Waboso England have someone who will always ensure opposition defences are scrambling.

On the evidence of his showing against Australia and his previous outing with Argentina, it does not feel hyperbolic to say England become anentirely different propositionwith the 23-year-old winger in the side.

England’s attack coach Lee Blackett knows all about Feyi-Waboso’s threats from their time together at Wasps and with Smith purring as he did on Sunday, the fly-half has the ability to unleash Borthwick’s most dangerous runner.
The trouble is, it has not happened often enough since Feyi-Waboso made his debut in early 2024.
Now that he is out of the rest of England’s November Tests, he will have managed just 17 appearances in England’s 36 matches since and including his debut come the end of the year.

A hamstring injury threatened his involvement this autumn, it was the same issue that forced him to miss the Six Nations and a shoulder problem that ruled him out of the Championship 12 months earlier.
He has not managed to string together more than five consecutive starts for England in his career.
Furbank, meanwhile, made his first appearance for England on Sunday since the 2024 autumn victory over Japan.

His run of bad luck with injuries has been astonishing – struck down by appendicitis when finally set to make his comeback over the summer – but the gracefulness with which he played against the Wallabies was a joy to watch.
Wearing white boots to match his kit only added to the impression that Furbank glides across the pitch.
His break to set up Jack van Poortvliet’s try was the champagne moment of an effervescent display, a reminder of what England have missed in his absence.
The hope must be that he is fit to face the All Blacks on Saturday week.

View image in fullscreenSteve Borthwick has tried many combinations since Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank last lined up for England together.Photograph: Mark Chappell/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock
Freeman’s “second debut” for England came in the same match in which Feyi-Waboso won his first cap, having been overlooked for the first 12 months of Borthwick’s tenure.
He went on to cement his status of one of the world’s leading wingers, before Borthwick preserved with attempting to reinvent him as an outside-centre.
Given Freeman has started the past three matches back on the right wing, it seems common sense has won the day.
In the two years since they all last lined up together, England have tried all manner of combinations.

Freddie Steward and Tom Roebuck enjoyed a degree of success when aerial supremacy was all the rage, but it does not feel like a coincidence that during England’s worst Six Nations campaign this year Feyi-Waboso was injured throughout, Furbank was overlooked and Freeman was often deployed at centre.
For thefirst defeat by Italy, not one of them appeared in the back three.
With 11 months before England’s World Cup opener against Tonga, however, Borthwick has his first-choice back three combination now staring him in the face.
The perfect blend of stylish playmaker at full-back, a robust, ultra-consistent performer on one wing, a game-breaker on the other.

Newsflash: Nvidia’s shares have dropped sharply at the start of trading in New York, as Wall Street gives its verdict on the company’s spying scandal.
Shares in the chip maker fell by almost 7.5% as soon as the opening bell rang out, as investors respond to the news that CEOJensenHuanghas admitted having an extramarital affair – reportedly with a Chinese spy.
That knocked the shares down to $172.75 each, down from $186.64 on Friday night.
That, by my maths, wipes $335bn offNvidia’svaluation, following the board’s decision to launch an independent investigation into whetherJensen Huanghas been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
It lowers the company’s value to around $4.16tn, down from $4.5tn on Friday night.
Too big – and too well-connected – to sack? One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to thinkJensen Huang, theNvidiaboss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation intothe alleged honeytrap spy scandal. The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power.
Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying aboutsuccession planning and “key person risk”or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US.
There isn’t even a Nvidia board member with the title of chair. Instead, a “lead director” is “designated annually by a majority of the independent directors”, which sounds like a formula for ensuring the attention remains wholly focused on Huang, the sole executive member.
It’s the American way, of course:the cult of the superstar founder or chief executiveruns deep and there is a fair argument that such set-ups encourage adventurous risk-taking in pursuit of grand corporate visions. But such governance arrangements lookunsuited to situations where the behaviour of the boss is under scrutiny and the role of the board itself is being examined.
The investigation will examine whether Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort” but the independent directors stressed there is now “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”
But legitimate questions don’t end there.Did Huang breakNvidia’s internal code of conduct? Did he mislead the board about his relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), the alleged Chinese spy? Was the board aware of US intelligence reports that Ms Huang had been hired by China’s ministry of state security to spy on the Nvidia boss, as reported by the New York Times? What security precautions were in place?Other boards in other countries might have insisted on suspending the boss until all the facts are in.
In the meantime, the defence of Huang from elsewhere has begun. “An honourable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it,”said Donald Trump. “Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership,”opined Shaun Maguire, a partner at Sequoia Capital, the powerful Silicon Valley investor. Yes, there is little doubt the US tech and political establishment would like this saga to end up in a series of bland conclusions about an everyday infidelity.
Nvidia’s board, however, would be wise not to rely on the “irreplaceable” consensus holding, or the political heat going away. This affair will be trawled over by newly empowered Democrats in Congress because it touches on how forcefully – or not – the administration has been enforcing its own national security restrictions on chip sales to China. This process will go on for months.Huang’s personal relationship with Trump will come under the spotlight like never before.
Will the Nvidia boss, even if he is cleared by the board’s investigation, still look so all-conquering by the end? His lobbying clout in Washington will be diminished. And Nvidia’s shareholders, if they’re doing the job properly, will surely insist on far greater visibility on where the company’s chips end up.
There may come a point where it is in Nvidia’s own interests to move on from the Jensen Huang era.The 63-year-old deserves all his accolades for spotting the enormous AI opportunity for the GPU chips that originated in the world of video games. The rise of Nvidia has been extraordinary. Butover-reliance on one individual is also a business risk.Time for some overdue succession planning – it may be needed.

Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny
Rebecca Bellan10:09 AM PST · November 9, 2026
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has never been quiet about his belief that the U.S. should continue selling AI chips to China, rather than shutting the country off from the technology. The revelation that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy threatens to complicate that argument.
The Financial Timesreported Friday on the relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. Jensen Huangadmittedto the affair and apologized in a memo to the company on Sunday. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company’s efforts to loosen chip export restrictions.
Nvidia’s independent directors, working with outside legal counsel, areinvestigatingthe matter, andCongress is already demanding answers.
The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia. Historically, China has been a big market for the company. It has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. In the three months ended July 26, Nvidia recorded $7.9 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, roughly 8% of total revenue.
Huang hasrepeatedly lobbiedthe U.S. government toexpand access to China, and some of his persuasion tactics have been successful. Huang met repeatedly with President Donald Trump and administration officials last year; afterward, the government reversed restrictions on Nvidia’s H20 chips and allowed exports of its more powerful H200 processors.
On numerous occasions, Huang has publicly lamented export controls, calling them a “failure” at a conference last year and saying in May that it was “not wise” for the U.S. and China to create two distinct AI ecosystems. He has also warned that shutting Nvidia out of China’s compute market would enable the country to develop its own AI chips to challenge Nvidia internationally.
China is already moving in that direction.Reuters reportedlast week that about 600,000 H200 chips are being held in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment to mainland China. Beijing is pushing AI companies to prioritize buying chips from Chinese companies instead.
The idea that Huang needed any encouragement in the form of an attractive woman to push for greater access to China seems like a stretch, particularly because his lobbying efforts predate their reported meeting at an Nvidia event in early 2024. At the end of the day, Huang is a salesman trying to dominate one of the world’s biggest AI markets.
Still, the allegations involving Alice Huang open new scrutiny of the company’s business relationships and could taint any assurances Nvidia offers that it can prevent sensitive technology from reaching unauthorized customers.
Once made, rumors of questionable allegiances can be hard to shake. Secretary of State Marco Rubioreportedlywarned officials close to Trump earlier this year about Huang’s relationship with an alleged spy. Even if Nvidia’s investigation finds that Huang didn’t share secrets with his paramour, the question is whether he’ll be able to convince Washington that Nvidia can still responsibly do business with China.
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.

Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy - BBC News
Image source,Bloomberg via Getty ImagesByArchie MitchellBusiness reporter
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmakerannounced an independent investigationwould be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 6% on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying "allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing,according to a New York Times report,external.
The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
After the investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Huang to continue leading the firm.
US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy".
However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company's market value.
While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened on a positive note on Monday after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting.
But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so central to the AI industry.
"Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC.
Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993.
Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but Huang decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company.
Huang's position vulnerable unlike other tech bosses
A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive.
Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him.
He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision.
By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies.
Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, "but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future."
The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched.
Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
Additional reporter by Samira Hussain, North America business correspondent.

The probe comes amid reports that Huang developed a close personal relationship with a Chinese business executive of a Nvidia partner company who allegedly passed information to Beijing. In a letter to employees, Huang admitted to not being faithful to his wife, but did not elaborate on the details of the relationship.
“NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully,” Huang said in the letter.
On Sunday, the firm announced the investigation. “The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said in a statement.
“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.”
The investigation puts Huang’s future in the spotlight at a company with a market capitalisation of $4.5 trillion. Huang is Nvidia’s fifth-largest shareholder, owning 3.6 percent of the company, according to LSEG data. However, Nvidia’s co-founder does not have majority voting control, unlike executives at other companies in the sector, such as Meta and SpaceX.
Thetech-heavyNasdaq was not affected by Nvidia’s downturn on Monday, with the index up 2.7 percent in early trading. Microsoft rose 2.2 percent, with chip maker AMD trading up over 10 percent on a new deal with Google and a stock analyst’s upgrade. Digital and e-commerce giant Amazon rose 3.8 percent.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 1.7 percent, and the S&P 500 rose 2.1 percent.
Analysts are sceptical that the controversy surrounding Huang will lead to him stepping down.
“Founder-led companies outperform because one person carries the vision,” Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founders 100 ETF, told Al Jazeera.
“Based on the current information, I would see that as highly improbable [that he is removed].”
This is not the first investigation into Huang’s relationships in recent months. In October, The New York Times reported that the CEO had a relationship with the alleged China operative, Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed. The two Huangs are not related.
Megaspeed, a data centre and cloud computing company, described itself as “a core business partner of NVIDIA’s computing power cloud business in the Asia-Pacific region” on its website.
US authorities investigated and concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, although the Chinese government pushed back against those allegations.
“The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.
The developments come amid a rough week forartificial intelligence (AI) investors on Wall Street.After markets settled following definitive results in the US midterm elections, candidates who ran on anti-AI platforms won overwhelmingly, giving Democrats, who are more critical of the AI industry than their Republican colleagues, control of both the House and the Senate in the new Congress.
Additionally, all but one of the data centre ballot measures seeking to restrict construction of new facilities across the US passed, sending shares of major AI firms tumbling on Thursday before they rose again on Friday.
“Jensen has two sets of enemies in Washington: China hawks who want the export door shut, and the crowd trying to stop the data centre buildout. The longer this drags, the stronger they get,” Monaghan told Al Jazeera.

Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence
LIVEUpdated9m agoLucy Campbell(now);Tom Ambrose,Graeme WeardenandLauren Almeida(earlier)Mon 9 Nov 2026 14.05 ESTFirst published on Mon 9 Nov 2026 02.09 ESTShareKey events

Jensen Huang, in the black T-shirt, pictured with Alice Huang in Taipei in May 2025Photograph: CTI/AFPTV/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJensen Huang, in the black T-shirt, pictured with Alice Huang in Taipei in May 2025Photograph: CTI/AFPTV/AFP/Getty ImagesFrom5h ago
Newsflash: Nvidia’s shares have dropped sharply at the start of trading in New York, as Wall Street gives its verdict on the company’s spying scandal.

Shares in the chip maker fell by almost 7.5% as soon as the opening bell rang out, as investors respond to the news that CEOJensenHuanghas admitted having an extramarital affair – reportedly with a Chinese spy.
That knocked the shares down to $172.75 each, down from $186.64 on Friday night.

That, by my maths, wipes $335bn offNvidia’svaluation, following the board’s decision to launch an independent investigation into whetherJensen Huanghas been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
It lowers the company’s value to around $4.16tn, down from $4.5tn on Friday night.
Too big – and too well-connected – to sack?

One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to thinkJensen Huang, theNvidiaboss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation intothe alleged honeytrap spy scandal.
The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power.
Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%.

On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying aboutsuccession planning and “key person risk”or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US.
There isn’t even a Nvidia board member with the title of chair.

Instead, a “lead director” is “designated annually by a majority of the independent directors”, which sounds like a formula for ensuring the attention remains wholly focused on Huang, the sole executive member.

It’s the American way, of course:the cult of the superstar founder or chief executiveruns deep and there is a fair argument that such set-ups encourage adventurous risk-taking in pursuit of grand corporate visions.
But such governance arrangements lookunsuited to situations where the behaviour of the boss is under scrutiny and the role of the board itself is being examined.

The investigation will examine whether Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort” but the independent directors stressed there is now “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”
But legitimate questions don’t end there.Did Huang breakNvidia’s internal code of conduct?
Did he mislead the board about his relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), the alleged Chinese spy?
Was the board aware of US intelligence reports that Ms Huang had been hired by China’s ministry of state security to spy on the Nvidia boss, as reported by the New York Times?
What security precautions were in place?Other boards in other countries might have insisted on suspending the boss until all the facts are in.
In the meantime, the defence of Huang from elsewhere has begun.

Apple’s $50 Intelligence Usage Packs extend access to some AI features
Logic Pro is Apple’s first app to charge for extended usage of Apple Intelligence.﻿
is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.
After publishing asupport article in early September outlining usage limitsfor some Apple Intelligence features, the company has updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for a one-time purchase price of $49.99, asspotted by9to5Mac. It has a built-in AI assistant to do things like “start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project.”
These Intelligence Usage Packs, as Apple calls them, will allow users to continue accessing certain Apple Intelligence features that have usage limits because they rely on cloud-based AI models from OpenAI or Google Gemini. The Usage Packs can only be used by the Apple Account that purchased them (Family Sharing isn’t supported) and,as Apple explains on its website, any unused additional usage will roll over from month to month, but will expire 12 months after it was purchased.
For Logic Pro, Apple says the usage limit is “impacted by the complexity of conversations you have with the assistant.” Users finding themselves running out of access can find the option to buy an Intelligence Usage Pack in the Intelligence Features > Show Usage section of the app’s main menu. Currently, only Logic Pro has the option to buy more usage, but it’s expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers that aregetting access to Apple’s AI chatbot.
