Steve Tandy warns Wales to be more ruthless after edgy win against Japan
Head coach wants more in New Zealand Test
Steve Tandy has admitted there is no hiding from his team’s below-par performance ⁠in their 28-21 homeNations Championshipvictory over Japan on Saturday where they looked flat at times and kept their ⁠opponents in the ⁠contest.
Wales recorded a bonus-point win as Josh Adams twice, Archie Griffin and Louis Rees-Zammit crossed, but they had to produce a desperate rearguard in the final moments to prevent Japan from an equalising score and a famous draw.
Scotland trail in All Blacks’ wake once more despite Ewan Ashman hat-trickRead more
“It’s a bonus-point win. It’s good to start,” Tandy said. “I can’t run away from the ⁠performance. There are elements we need to improve. I thought we’d be better. We ​weren’t ruthless enough.”
Tandy suggested rust may ‌have been to blame ‌as Wales played their first Test since July.
“Getting a hit out for the ‌first time since the summer, it does get clunky,” he said. “It helps to review after a bonus point win. We’ll enjoy it but the beauty of this group is the hunger to get better quicker. We’ll definitely have to do that.”
Next up for Wales are New Zealand next weekend and Australia. Tandy ‌knows his side cannot afford to offer up cheap opportunities in those games.
“We’d go seven points up and there’d be a ​sloppy moment,” he said. “There was some excitement in what we tried to do. Japan were effective close to the line. We managed the game well outside of that. Defensively, we improved.”
Wales have now won two of their four Nations Championship games, but stay fifth in the northern hemisphere standings.
Quick GuideFrance and South Africa win but at a cost for Les BleusShow
Francestormed back to the top of the Northern Hemisphere Nations Championship table with a dominant but flawed 54-17 victory overFijion Saturday.
Victory came at a cost, with the fly-half Romain Ntamack, alongside captain Antoine Dupont at half-back for the first time since March 2025, seemingly dislocating his shoulder in the buildup to France’s third try.
With Mathieu Jalibert already out injured, Les Bleus will face world champions South Africa next week without either of their best No 10s.
They will also need to put in a vastly improved showing to stand any chance of avoiding a 10th defeat in their last 11 clashes with the Springboks.
Props Jean-Baptiste Gros and Sipili Falatea, wing Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, centre Kalvin Gourgues, full-back Theo Attissogbe, replacement forward Charles Ollivon and Dupont crossed the whitewash, with a penalty try making it eight scores for the hosts.
They are two points ahead of Ireland in the standings ahead of England’s clash with Australia on Sunday.
Fiji, who started the match with 10 France-based players, including their entire backline, were typically physical but slumped to a fourth straight defeat in the inaugural Nations Championship.
Their much-vaunted backs struggled to fire, although centre Vinaya Habosi beat four defenders to score and Selestino Ravutaumada added a second consolation try. The Top 14’s most prolific finisher, Jiuta Wainiqolo, who was playing in his adopted home, was unable to make an impact, though.
EarlierSouth Africastrolled past an injury-hit ⁠Italywith a 66-7 win in Saturday’s Nations Championship meeting in ⁠Turin, where the ⁠fly-half ​Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu scored the first of nine Springbok tries and added ⁠another 21 points from a perfect kicking display.
South Africa ran in six ⁠tries in an utterly dominant opening half. ​Hooker Malcolm Marx ‌went over ‌twice, adding to scores by Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van ‌den Berg and the captain Siya Kolisi and Damian Willemse, with Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicking all six conversions having opened the scoring with a penalty.
Wilco Louw added another try after ‌the break before Italy finally got off the mark with Federico Ruzza’s ​try converted by Tommaso Allan. Springbok wing Ethan Hooker ran in the final score on the stroke of full-time.Agencies
Japan’s coach, Eddie Jones, felt it was a missed opportunity for his ⁠side, who had 62% of the possession but struggled with entries ​into the Wales 22.
“That ​could have been a historic ​win for us,” Jones said. “But you’ve got to be good enough ​to take advantage ‌of those mistakes. ​We weren’t quite ​good enough. It was a missed opportunity.
“I’m proud of my team. We had a young team, but they stuck at it. We had a few times where we didn’t take chances and Wales did.”

A 55-Year-Old Math Problem Was Solved—This Time by Humans | WIREDSkip to main content
The original versionofthis storyappeared inQuanta Magazine.
The late RonaldGraham wore two hats. He was arenowned mathematicianand, at one time, president of the American Mathematical Society. He was also a serious juggler and president of the International Jugglers’ Association. “He loved tricks,” said Fan Chung, a mathematician at UC San Diego who was married to Graham. “You know, spinning a ball, spinning a coat hanger, spinning several balls together, throwing pens against the wall.”
Sometimes Graham wore both hats at once. “It’s interesting, in fact, that many mathematicians and computer scientists have an interest in juggling,” he said in a1980 television interview. “I think it’s the search for patterns and structure that is responsible for this.”
He would go on to write numerous papers,some with Chung, on the mathematics of juggling. But back in 1971, decades before he made that connection explicit, he posed a question that some mathematicians now say might have been inspired by juggling, too.
Start with a random set of different integers, not including zero. Can you always rearrange them so that if you add up the first two numbers, then the first three, then the first four, and so on, every “partial sum” turns out different? In the language of juggling, this would mean that if each ball stays in the air for a different amount of time, you can always find an order to throw them in such that two balls won’tcome crashing downon the same beat—which would ruin the act.
If the numbers are all positive, then the answer to Graham’s question is obviously yes: The sums will always grow larger as you add more numbers. Similarly, if there are both positive and negative numbers in the mix, the answer is also known to be yes. But what if the numbers livein a finite world—like numbers wrapped around a clock, which repeat after a certain count?
The late mathematician Ronald Graham was also a skilled juggler.Photograph: Peter Vidor
That’s what Graham wanted to know. He conjectured that the answer should still be yes. It often happens, he figured, that even when dealing with rigid constraints, you can still find enough flexibility to construct special patternsor structures—just as it’s usually possible to find a valid sudoku board orLatin square(another kind of puzzle) despite their many rules. “It fits nicely in all these questions about designs and about very symmetric structures,” said Noga Alon, a mathematician at Princeton University. But for decades, no one could prove Graham’s intuition to be true.
That changed recently, when several young mathematicians picked up the balls. In a proof that spanned four papers andvarious fields of mathematics, they finally resolved Graham’s rearrangement conjecture. Thefinal paper, by Lisa Sauermann of the University of Bonn and Huy Tuan Pham of the University of Chicago, appeared in February 2026, officially closing the problem.
Across the papers, one theme prevailed: thepower of randomnessto draw out patterns. As Alon put it, “It’s the power of collaboration, the power of the young generation, the power of probabilistic methods” that solved the problem.
Alp Müyesser, amathematician at the University of Oxford, often finds himself drawn to problems whose solutions need two ingredients: a random process and something extra as well. After solving one such problem in 2022 while he was still a graduate student, he encountered Graham’s conjecture and realized that his just-finished proof could help there, too.
Alp Müyesser enjoys thinking about problems that require him to combine randomness with something else.Photograph: Kangxin Chen
The conjecture is set in the world of clock arithmetic. You start by placing the whole numbers on anumber line, then you wrap the line around the face of a clock so that the numbers repeat after some prime number,p. Saypis 7, for instance. In this setting, 0, 7, 14, and all other multiples of 7 are equivalent—meaning that you can add two positive numbers (like 3 and 4) and get zero.
Graham asked the following: If you pick any set of nonzero numbers off this number line (for anyp), can you always rearrange them so that the partial sums you get are all different?
The challenge depends on how big your set is compared top. Themore numbersyou pick, the more sums there are to manage. But if you choose fewer numbers, there will be fewer ways to rearrange them. These different cases inspire different approaches.
Müyesser, along with his former adviser, Alexey Pokrovskiy of University College London, tackled the case where your set includes almost every possible number up top. With sets this large, it can be extremely hard to construct a valid ordering. But it turned out that starting witha random orderingcan bring you most of the way there.
“Computer scientists often call this a ‘finding the hay in the haystack’ problem,” Müyesser said. You might know that lots of good orderings are out there, but actually finding one is hard. “If you do it randomly, it’s likely going to work, but it’s hard to explicitly describe what the solution is supposed to look like.”
Müyesser and Pokrovskiy needed to ensure that no sequence of numbers anywhere in the ordering added up to zero. Otherwise, adding those numbers to the previous partial sum would repeat that sum.
A completely random ordering might have a few of thesetroublesome sequences. So Müyesser and Pokrovskiy first set aside a few specially chosen numbers from the set, then randomly scrambled the rest. They scanned their random ordering for any problems; if they came across an interval that added up to zero, they could insert one of the spare numbers to change it. In 2022, theyposted their solution, though it was hidden in a paper that focused on applying the same technique to a more general problem.
A couple of years later, Noah Kravitz of Oxford, unaware of Müyesser and Pokrovskiy’s solution, stumbled on Graham’s conjecture in an online archive of unsolved problems. “I saw there was an open problem, and I was like, it’sembarrassing for humanitythat we don’t know this,” Kravitz said. “This situation just had to be rectified.”
He decided to approach the conjecture from the opposite end. Together with Benjamin Bedert of Oxford, he considered the case where the set of numbers is tiny compared top—for instance, Alon said, if you have a set of 100 numbers wherepis 1 billion.

Swansea mum tries to raise £2.95m for son's dementia treatment - BBC News
Image source,Tammy McDaidImage caption,
Tate's mum Tammy McDaid needs £3m for life-saving treatment for her child
The mum of a five-year-old boy with a rare form of dementia has to pay almost £3m for his life saving treatment.
Tate McDaid, from Swansea, was diagnosed with Sanfilippo Syndrome - a form of dementia that just over 100 UK children have -when he was four.
In September, the first gene therapy to treat the condition in children was approved in the US.
His mum Tammy said she spent "months praying" for its approval but discovered the treatment is to set cost £2.95 million per child, with it unclear how families outside the US can fund this.
Health officials from Wales are currently talking to those in the US to see what potential access pathways there are for Tate.
"I was excited when the treatment initially got approved but then reality hit hard the next day," Tammy said.
This was when she readthe US price for the one-time treatment,externalhad been set at $3.95 million.
Tammy contacted Ultragenyx, who developed the treatment, in the hope of understanding how families outside the US, who do not have health insurance there, will cover the costs.
"We understand what they are charging for American citizens, but they've got health insurance," she added.
"Not even just the UK, but everyone else in the world looking for this treatment."
Explaining how the US approved drug, FAYUVI, would work for families outside the US, Ultragenyx said: "There is not a single estimate we can provide for the total cost of care for an international patient, as those costs would depend on the patient's individual medical needs and the treating institution."
TheSociety for Mucopolysaccharide Diseases,external, a charity which helps children living with Sanfilippo Syndrome, said about 140 children in the UK have the condition.
There is currently no cure for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A, also called Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), but the new drug could delay its onset, and allow Tate to remain active for longer.
The condition, described as "childhood Alzheimer's" or "childhood dementia" due to its neurodegenerative nature, causes the gradual loss of abilities, such as walking and eating.
It can progress more rapidly after the age of five, which is why Tammy said "it's really a battle of time" for her to raise enough money to get her son the treatment that is not available yet in the UK.
She said: "If a millionaire turned around tomorrow and gave us the money, we'd go to the US straight away."
With Tate turning six this month, Tammy doesn't believe time is on their side.
"Tate is already shown signs of cognitive decline," she added.
"The older he gets the less the treatment will work and the more ability he will lose in the process.
"I feel like we are at a turning point and I'm petrified."
Tammy said the new drug could help her son to keep his mobility for longer
Describing him as "the happiest little man" who is "blissfully unaware" of his problems, Tammy explained how important Tate's mobility is to him.
"He doesn't speak, he's never spoken. But his mobility is everything to him and that is why I'm fighting for it," she said.
Tammy began raising money before the new drug was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and now has more than £160,000.
But this covers only about 5% of the total estimated cost of the treatment.
"Unfortunately, we're in a world where we need millions, not hundreds of thousands," she added.
"I'm just really hoping by some miracle the pharmaceutical company eventually come back to us and say they can do it for a little bit cheaper, but it's still going to be in the millions."
Tate's mum Tammy has raised more than £160,000 so far but hopes to reach £2.95 million
Ultragenyx said: "We are pursuing a global regulatory strategy, and FDA approval is an important first step in our long-term goal of bringing this treatment option to families around the world.
"We also understand the urgency families affected by Sanfilippo syndrome Type A face in identifying treatment options and why some may consider travelling to the US to access gene therapy.
"We recommend families work with their child's healthcare provider to understand what potential access pathways may exist before assuming this is their only option."
Staff from the Noah's Ark Children's Hospital in Cardiff are currently discussing this with officials in the US on the family's behalf.

When Carter Stevens tells people he makes six figures a year digging through dumpsters, they often assume he's "blowing smoke," he says.
Not everyone sees dollar signs in a brimming dumpster. But Stevens earned roughly $140,000 in total sales between September 2025 and September 2026 by salvaging trashed items, cleaning them up and selling them on platforms like eBay and Facebook Marketplace, according to documents reviewed by CNBC Make It.
Stevens primarily operates near office parks and luxury condominiums around Nashville, Tennessee. Since March 2024, when he started dumpster diving, he's found and sold hand-crafted Persian rugs, high-end office chairs and even samurai swords, he says. Trash-picking helps him keep his shipping costs low, he adds: Some of his supplies, like cardboard boxes and packing tape, also come from dumpsters, enough that he doesn't have to pay for them approximately "90% of the time."
"The amount of waste in this country that you'll find is unbelievable. We throw so much stuff out," says Stevens, 31.
Sometimes, Stevens asks a building for permission to go through its trash, marketing himself as a junk removal service. In that way, his job is similar — though not identical, because he generally only takes what he can sell, he says — to other entrepreneurs across the U.S. who follow advice in Reddit threads or YouTube tutorials to launchjunk removal side hustles or full-time businesses. There are around10,000 junk removal businessesacross the U.S., according to the Better Business Bureau. They range in scale from independent side hustles to national companies like1-800-GOT-JUNK, which touts more than 150 franchise locations.
Other times, Stevens finds himself neck deep in rubbish, ducking concerned security guards, peeling away actual trash and rotting food in the hope of uncovering discarded treasure, he says. He tries to avoid sneaking around and keeps an eye out for "no trespassing" signs. He'd rather leave items behind if a property owner or security guard tells him to vacate the premises, he says.
Even Stevens expresses surprise at how much money he's made, saying he doesn't necessarily think his annual income is sustainable. When he "stumbled into" dumpster diving, he was approximately $12,000 in debt after years of poor spending habits fueled partially by a drug addiction, a stark change from his affluent childhood, he says.
"I dug myself out of a hole. I built up my savings. I really did much more than I thought was possible," says Stevens.
Battling addiction, turning trash into 'a little bit of money'
Stevens, a Nashville native, is the son of a five-time Grammy Award-winning producer of country and gospel music who has worked with artists like Blake Shelton and Carrie Underwood. His life took a turn in college when he developed an addiction to prescription Adderall, leading him to drop out partway through his senior year in 2018, he says.
His lack of a college degree made landing full-time work a challenge. He says his parents can afford to support him financially, and they've done so in specific emergency occasions. But mostly, his father wants his kids to learn to fend for themselves, he says: "He will let me sit on the coals for the sake of learning how to swim. That's taught me a lot [and] given me a lot of valuable skills and a tough mentality."
Unemployed, Stevens started combing through thrift shops and Goodwill clothing racks for vintage apparel to sell on eBay. He was inspired by YouTube influencers like Rick Senko, he says, whose Fort Lauderdale, Florida-basedclothing resale business Technsports brought in $6.5 millionin annual revenue as recently as 2024.
Carter Stevens is a Nashville-based dumpster diver.Source: CNBC Make It
But Stevens' returns were inconsistent, and he often spent his profits on drugs or luxury shopping sprees, he says. After his parents funded a rehab stint in 2021 — helping him "quit doing the hard drugs," he says — he spent his money chasing other dopamine hits. Those indulgences included a $1,200 pair of Christian Dior Birkenstock sandals, an 85-inch flat-screen television and a $30,000 down payment on a Mercedes-AMG sedan that he later lost because he couldn't afford the total cost, he says.
By June 2023, he could no longer afford to pay rent, so he lived in a rented storage unit until the business's security found and evicted him, and then stayed in his Nissan Sentra for three weeks, he says. Homelessness shocked him into learning to manage his "reckless" spending habits, he says: "Being punished by your own spending addiction was a wringer that I promised myself I can't be put through again."
In October 2023, a cousin lent him money to start renting an apartment, and Stevens worked to stick to a sensible enough budget for his thrifting income to cover future rent and basic expenses, he says. Five months later, he found a discarded pair of black Nike Air Force Ones in good condition next to a gas station pump. He took them home, sanitized them and sold them online for $35, he says.
"That was the first time I had ever found something that was trash and sold it and made a little bit of money," says Stevens.
'Almost every piece of furniture in my apartment came from a dumpster'
Once he started dumpster diving, Stevens was hooked "because I never stopped finding good stuff in these dumpsters," he says.
His biggest score to date: dozens of discarded Steelcase office chairs, worth $1,000-plus each when new, outside an overflowing office park dumpster, he says. He got his car — by this point, a used pickup truck and a self-built trailer — and hauled away 190 chairs to list online at hundreds of dollars apiece. He sold the majority of them in bulk transactions on Facebook Marketplace for $17,000, and brought in an additional $10,600 selling the remaining chairs individually, documents show.

400,000-year-old teeth reveal a stunning twist in human evolution
Date:November 5, 2026Source:The ConversationSummary:A groundbreaking discovery is rewriting the story of human evolution, revealing that an ancient human species once thought to be an evolutionary dead end may have left genetic traces in people alive today. By extracting proteins from 400,000-year-old Homo erectus teeth discovered in China, scientists uncovered evidence suggesting that these early humans interbred with Denisovans, another mysterious ancient human group. That genetic connection may have eventually reached modern populations in the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and other parts of Southeast Asia.Share:FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedINEmailFULL STORYAncient proteins from 400,000-year-old teeth reveal that Homo erectus may have left a hidden genetic legacy in modern humans, rewriting our evolutionary family tree. Credit: Shutterstock
For most of the 20th century, the model of human origins was a tree: with the trunk dividing into branches, and then twigs. Each species of human relative (hominin) was a neat, single branch.
As an undergraduate, I was taught thatHomo sapienswas one of these branchesthat emerged in Africa, spread across the world, and displaced every archaic human it encountered.
Neanderthals,Homo erectus, and other ancient relatives were evolutionary dead ends – unfortunate cousins who left no descendants. In the 30 years since I left university, those early lessons are now radically revised.
That neat replacement story is now comprehensively wrong, largely thanks to studies like the onepublished inNatureby Qiaomei Fu from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and colleagues. The paper achieves something that would have seemed impossible a decade ago: it recovers meaningful biological information fromH. erectusfossils far too old for DNA.
Instead of genetic sequences, the team extracted ancient proteins from the enamel of six teeth from three Chinese sites – Zhoukoudian (which, in the early 20th century, produced fossil remains known as “Peking Man”), Hexian and Sunjiadong – all dating to around 400,000 years ago.
Homo erectusis widely regarded as the first hominin to leave Africa; the evidence suggests this species had moved into Eurasia nearly two million years ago. It remains the most geographically widespread human ancestor that ever lived. The new study indicates thatHomo erectusexchanged genes (probably through interbreeding) with Denisovans in East Asia roughly 400,000 years ago.
The study suggests that some of that genetic legacy, it now appears, was passed on to living people in the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and across south-east Asia.
Tooth enamel is the hardest tissue in the body, and its proteins survive long after DNA has degraded beyond recovery. What the team found in those proteins is striking. All six specimens share a previously unknown amino acid variant – a tiny molecular signature, a single letter changed in the protein sequence, never seen in any other hominin alive or dead.
This variant clusters these east AsianH. erectusinto a distinct group, confirming their identity and settling a long-running debate about whether the unusual Hexian fossils wereH. erectusat all. A second variant they share, however, is not unique toH. erectus.
It also appears in Denisovans – a mysterious archaic (non-Homo sapiens) human group known mainly from a cave in Siberia. The corresponding genetic variant turns up in living people at frequencies of 21% in the Philippines and about 1% in India, distributed in a pattern that matches what we’d expect if it entered modern humans via Denisovan ancestry.
The most reasonable interpretation is thatH. erectuspopulations in east Asia passed this variant to Denisovans through interbreeding, and Denisovans laterpassed it onto the ancestors of modern south-east Asians and Oceanians. This transfer of genetic material from one species to another is known as introgression.
The lineage we once thought was a dead end has, it turns out, left a small but detectable trace in living human genomes – a molecular thread connecting a Peking Man tooth to living people in Asia.
But the significance of today’s paper extends well beyond the specific variant or the specific populations involved. What it really shows is that interbreeding between archaic human lineages was not exceptional. It was routine.
Every major hominin lineage we have been able to examine genomically shows admixture. Modern humans outside Africa carry roughly 2% Neanderthal DNA. Papuans and Aboriginal Australians carry an additional 2–5% Denisovan ancestry.
West African populations carry genetic signatures from anunidentified archaic lineage. Even Denisovans themselves, as today’s study adds further weight to, received gene flow from something older and more diverged — likelyH. erectus.
A 2019 reviewin the American Journal of Physical Anthropology documents at least three distinct introgression events from Denisovan-like populations into south-east Asian and Oceanic ancestors alone, some occurring as recently as 20,000 years ago. The picture is not one of clean lineages but of a tangled web of contact and exchange extending across millions of years.
The implications are far-reaching. Our genomes are not the product of a single unbroken lineage emerging from Africa. They are mosaics, assembled from contributions by multiple archaic groups, each adapted to its own regional environment.
Some of the Denisovan-derived variants in Papuan genomes, for instance,appear to influence immune function. TheH. erectus-derived variant identified today has unknown functional consequences – that remains an open question – but the precedent from other gene variants that have introgressed (genes that have passed from one species into another) suggests that adaptation to new environments may have been part of the story.
Perhaps most intriguing is what the new paper implies about all the populations we cannot yet study.H. erectussurvived in Indonesia until perhaps 100,000 years ago.Homo floresiensis, the diminutive “hobbit” species, was present on Flores when modern humans arrived. Another human lineage,Homo luzonensis, occupied the Philippines.

England’s Test against Australia will be a big moment for (clockwise from top left) Steve Borthwick, Ben Curry, Fin Smith and Maro Itoje.Composite: Guardian Design; NurPhoto/Getty Images; RFU/Getty Images; Camerasport/Getty Images; Nations Championship/Getty Images;View image in fullscreenEngland’s Test against Australia will be a big moment for (clockwise from top left) Steve Borthwick, Ben Curry, Fin Smith and Maro Itoje.Composite: Guardian Design; NurPhoto/Getty Images; RFU/Getty Images; Camerasport/Getty Images; Nations Championship/Getty Images;
Injury crises and Borthwick under scrutiny: it’s that time of year again for England rugby
Sunday’s hosts need to stop looking for excuses and focus on what they can control to kick off the Nations Championship against battle-hardened Australia
Several things are increasingly guaranteed from an English rugby perspective around this time of year. Bang on cue the injury news and the weather both start to worsen. Cracks in the relationship between the players and their head coach, in this case Steve Borthwick, begin to surface. And as the crowds stream up from Twickenham railway station past the biltong and burger stalls, no one has much idea what to expect.
This year it has been the same old story. Particularly on the injury front.If Tom Curry, Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland had not all been hurt on the Bagshot training pitch, all three would probably be in England’s matchday 23. With Guy Pepper, Benhard van Rensburg, Sam Underhill, Kepu Tuipulotu and Chandler Cunningham-South also out of the running, the squad is not quite as fizzing with energy and dynamism as it might be.
Tom Curry a major injury doubt for England with twin Ben poised to step up against AustraliaRead more
And Borthwick, not for the first time, is back under scrutiny. According to a well-sourced report in the Times, his players sought a clear-the-air meeting in Argentina in July having allegedly grown unhappy with the former England captain’s man management and lack of empathy. It makes Sunday’s openingNations ChampionshipTest against Australia even more of a must-win game than was already the case.
All this, ironically, in the same week that the Rugby Football Union restated itsdesire for Borthwick to remain in his postthrough to the World Cup. Perhaps officials got wind of the impending story. Or, again not for the first time, maybe the chief executive, Bill Sweeney, has once more backed the wrong horse, having jettisoned Eddie Jones barely nine months before the last World Cup.
What a diplomatic mess, albeit a wearily familiar one. It had already been a curious week before these latest allegations surfaced. Sweeney even mentioned a stat suggesting England are the world’s second-best side when they keep 15 players on the field but only eighth or ninth when down to 14 or fewer. No shit, Sherlock. More pertinent, surely, is how England become sufficiently composed under pressure to avoid leaking costly penalties or cards.
Back in Santiago del Estero in July Borthwick opted to blame the “negativity committee” in the media for raising the subject after the game. Given his team had just lost four men to the sin-bin in the second half and barely clung on to win, it felt distinctly odd at the time. Given the newly reported context it now makes more sense.
View image in fullscreenArgentina's Boris Wenger challenges Ollie Chessum during July’s narrow England win.Photograph: Fernando Ariaz/Reuters
The truth, then and now, is that something doesn’t feel entirely right about England, whether it be elements of the gameplan, the coaching blend, certain selections, cultural alignment or all of the above. They certainly need to find an urgent cure for the rampaging yellow fever that has cost them 14 yellow cards, plus one red, in 2026 to date. When they are in control of their own destiny, as opposed to scrambling desperately in their own 22, rugby becomes a different game.
Thissame fixture 12 months agowas, by the end, a prime example. Australia arrived tired and lacking a few key men and the home side, with six British & Irish Lions arriving off the bench, stretched clear to record a comfortable 25-7 win, the highlight being an eye-catching score from – who else? – Henry Pollock.
That result also extended England’s winning run to eight Tests. This year, though, their star has waned significantly, with only two wins –against a below-par Fijiandthe Pumas– in their past seven Tests. Which is what has lent an extra frisson to this November even before the RFU’s “nothing to see here” messaging.
What price such corporate froth on Monday morning should Australia get up as they so memorably did in London in 2024? Or if Japan and Jones, havinglost only 35-32 to the Wallabiesin August, also take a sharp Samurai sword to English pretensions next Saturday? Staging the Nations Championship finals weekend at Allianz Stadium is all fine and dandy until the party hosts find themselves locked out in the communal hallway while the proper action is going on inside.
The alternative scenario, of course, involves the Wallabies being splattered across the sweet chariot’s windshield, the Brave Blossoms being scrummaged and mauled off the park and the All Blacks being turned over for the second successive autumn. If France, Ireland and Scotland all have a mixed month it is still possible Borthwick’s unhappy campers could make the inaugural Nations Championship final and enter 2027 with rather more in the way of optimism.
Place your chips and roll those dice. The midterm elections in the US have also just underlined how radically things can alter virtually overnight. But if England’s men want to rank among the world’s leading four teams again, let alone the top two, they need to find some kind of positive injection next year, whether in terms of selection, personnel or fresh coaching ideas.
View image in fullscreenFraser McReight, pictured in action against France in July, is a threat England must contain.Photograph: Darren England/EPA
It may not matter on Sunday if England’s front five get an early grip, the outstanding Fraser McReight is countered at the breakdown and the Wallabies are mauled halfway back to Wollongong but there is a bigger picture to be considered as well. Among other things, Borthwick is taking a calculated gamble

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time never gets old
The franchise has evolved since 1998, but the first 3D Zelda stands up incredibly well in its Switch 2 remake.
Image: NintendoPart OfAll the news about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remakesee all updatesAndrew Webster
is an entertainment editor covering streaming, virtual worlds, and every single Pokémon video game. Andrew joined The Verge in 2012, writing over 4,000 stories.
Breath of the Wildchanged everything. Two decades afterThe Legend of Zeldamade the transformational shift to 3D,Breath of the Wildreinvigorated the franchisewith an open-ended adventure that was built around player freedom and expression. Instead of following a set path, players could go wherever they wanted and tackle challenges in a variety of ways. That philosophy filtered down to subsequent games, letting players author their own creative solutions to puzzles in titles likeTears of the KingdomandEchoes of Wisdom. As a result,Zeldahas never been bigger, and the traditional, more linearZeldagames had become a thing of the past. Or so it seemed.
For one of the biggest Switch 2 exclusives so far, Nintendo has gone back toOcarina of Time, which originally launched on the N64 in 1998. It’s one of the most influential and revered games in the long-running franchise, a game that showed that the classicZeldaformula — one that used a large world to connect a handful of intricate, puzzle-filled dungeons, creating a grand adventure — could work in three dimensions. NowOcarinahas been remade for the Switch 2 in a way that accomplishes exactly what a good remake is designed to do: preserve the core of the original experience while making it more accessible for modern audiences. And it shows there’s still some life left in the traditionalZeldaformula.
The story remains unchanged from the original. It’s a third-person action-adventure game where you play as a little forest dweller named Link who gets pulled into an adventure to save the fantasy realm of Hyrule from a villain named Ganondorf. That’s true of basically everyZeldatitle, and here the twist comes from a musical instrument (the titular flute-like ocarina) imbued with magical powers. Over the course of the game you learn songs that can change the weather, warp you across the landscape, mess with the flow of time, and more.
The originalOcarinawas renowned both for its large 3D world and for the intricacy of its dungeons, which required using the ocarina, along with various other items, to solve puzzles in clever ways. At a certain point you’re even jumping back and forth in time, navigating spaces as both tiny Link and his adult version. The challenge steadily grows in complexity right up until you face Ganondorf in his castle, forcing you to use a huge range of items at your disposal.
The most notable difference in the remake is how it looks. Gone are the blocky, fuzzy N64-era graphics, which have been replaced with something that blurs the line between fantasy art and realism. While it’s not a fully open world likeBreath of the Wild, this version of Hyrule, which has a large open field that connects a series of dungeons and villages, is still incredibly lifelike; everything from rushing water in a lake to the swaying grass outside of a ranch looks and moves in realistic ways. The flip side is that, while the characters are more detailed than before, they’ve been rendered witha style inspired by puppets and stage shows. It’s a tricky balancing act that the game mostly nails. The characters look like exaggerated caricatures, but at the same time they’re imbued with such a level of detail that they don’t feel out of place against the more realistic backdrops. Link is the best example; while his face almost looks like a porcelain figure, his outfit is like something a real adventurer would wear, made by weaving together grasses found in Kokiri Forest, where he lives.
It looks great in practice — althoughOcarinadoes suffer from some frustratingly dark areas, like in most modern games — and it also sets the remake apart from the rest of modernZeldaadventures. TheBreath of the Wildline has a fantastical, Studio Ghibli-inspired look, whilethe top-down spinoffs have cutesy, toylike graphics.Ocarinasplits the difference and comes out looking like something distinct, yet unmistakablyZelda. The Switch 2 graphics also do a great job of heightening the emotion. There’s an incredible sense of grandeur when you first walk into the stark Temple of Time, with a single ray of light illuminating the dark interior. Iconic moments like wandering blindly through the desert take on a new sense of tension and terror because of how the game looks as sand whips around you, obscuring your view of the harsh landscape. Fighting Dark Link on a foggy, desolate beach was enough to get my heart racing.
Perhaps more important than the visual update is a number of smart gameplay changes. Early 3D games can be awkward to play now because designers were still working out how best to navigate 3D spaces. TheOcarinaremake fixes this in a few ways. For one thing, you now have free camera control, making it possible to look anywhere by moving the right stick, just like in any modern game. This makes it easier to keep your eye on enemies around you or spot important details for solving a puzzle. The game now also lets you jump whenever you want — in the original Link could only jump at designated points — which makes moving around in spaces feel less restrictive. Other modern touches include being able to equip items quickly with the D-pad instead of having to go to the pause menu, and the “threads of time,” which is a fancy name for a tool that tracks your quests so you can more easily figure out what to do next.
As an example of how much these tweaks can impact the experience, let’s revisit the infamous Water Temple. Over the years sinceOcarina of Timefirst launched, this dungeon has become known primarily for being extremely difficult. It involves constantly playing a song to make the water rise and fall so you can access different levels, while also frequently equipping iron boots that cause Link to sink to the bottom when necessary. fact_units.text: A 55-Year-Old Math Problem Was Solved—This Time by Humans | WIREDSkip to main content
He was arenowned mathematicianand, at one time, president of the American Mathematical Society.
He was also a serious juggler and president of the International Jugglers’ Association.
“He loved tricks,” said Fan Chung, a mathematician at UC San Diego who was married to Graham.
“You know, spinning a ball, spinning a coat hanger, spinning several balls together, throwing pens against the wall.”
“It’s interesting, in fact, that many mathematicians and computer scientists have an interest in juggling,” he said in a1980 television interview.
“I think it’s the search for patterns and structure that is responsible for this.”
He would go on to write numerous papers,some with Chung, on the mathematics of juggling.
But back in 1971, decades before he made that connection explicit, he posed a question that some mathematicians now say might have been inspired by juggling, too.
Start with a random set of different integers, not including zero.
Can you always rearrange them so that if you add up the first two numbers, then the first three, then the first four, and so on, every “partial sum” turns out different?

In the language of juggling, this would mean that if each ball stays in the air for a different amount of time, you can always find an order to throw them in such that two balls won’tcome crashing downon the same beat—which would ruin the act.
If the numbers are all positive, then the answer to Graham’s question is obviously yes: The sums will always grow larger as you add more numbers.
Similarly, if there are both positive and negative numbers in the mix, the answer is also known to be yes.
But what if the numbers livein a finite world—like numbers wrapped around a clock, which repeat after a certain count?
The late mathematician Ronald Graham was also a skilled juggler.Photograph: Peter Vidor
He conjectured that the answer should still be yes.

It often happens, he figured, that even when dealing with rigid constraints, you can still find enough flexibility to construct special patternsor structures—just as it’s usually possible to find a valid sudoku board orLatin square(another kind of puzzle) despite their many rules.
“It fits nicely in all these questions about designs and about very symmetric structures,” said Noga Alon, a mathematician at Princeton University.
But for decades, no one could prove Graham’s intuition to be true.
That changed recently, when several young mathematicians picked up the balls.
In a proof that spanned four papers andvarious fields of mathematics, they finally resolved Graham’s rearrangement conjecture.
Thefinal paper, by Lisa Sauermann of the University of Bonn and Huy Tuan Pham of the University of Chicago, appeared in February 2026, officially closing the problem.
Across the papers, one theme prevailed: thepower of randomnessto draw out patterns.
As Alon put it, “It’s the power of collaboration, the power of the young generation, the power of probabilistic methods” that solved the problem.
Alp Müyesser, amathematician at the University of Oxford, often finds himself drawn to problems whose solutions need two ingredients: a random process and something extra as well.
After solving one such problem in 2022 while he was still a graduate student, he encountered Graham’s conjecture and realized that his just-finished proof could help there, too.
Alp Müyesser enjoys thinking about problems that require him to combine randomness with something else.Photograph: Kangxin Chen
The conjecture is set in the world of clock arithmetic.
You start by placing the whole numbers on anumber line, then you wrap the line around the face of a clock so that the numbers repeat after some prime number,p.
In this setting, 0, 7, 14, and all other multiples of 7 are equivalent—meaning that you can add two positive numbers (like 3 and 4) and get zero.
Graham asked the following: If you pick any set of nonzero numbers off this number line (for anyp), can you always rearrange them so that the partial sums you get are all different?
The challenge depends on how big your set is compared top.
Themore numbersyou pick, the more sums there are to manage.
But if you choose fewer numbers, there will be fewer ways to rearrange them.
Müyesser, along with his former adviser, Alexey Pokrovskiy of University College London, tackled the case where your set includes almost every possible number up top.
With sets this large, it can be extremely hard to construct a valid ordering.
But it turned out that starting witha random orderingcan bring you most of the way there.
“Computer scientists often call this a ‘finding the hay in the haystack’ problem,” Müyesser said.
You might know that lots of good orderings are out there, but actually finding one is hard.

article.title: Vụ xả súng kinh hoàng tại Kraków: Sáu người thiệt mạng và bối cảnh điều tra
article.summary: Một tay súng đã nổ súng ngẫu nhiên tại quảng trường lịch sử ở Kraków, Ba Lan, khiến sáu người thiệt mạng và nhiều người bị thương. Nhà chức trách nhận định nghi phạm mang tư tưởng cực đoan và cuộc điều tra vẫn đang tiếp tục mở rộng.
body: Vào chiều thứ Bảy, một vụ xả súng nghiêm trọng đã xảy ra tại Quảng trường Chợ chính ở thành phố Kraków, Ba Lan. Theo nhà chức trách, một nghi phạm đã lái xe vào khu vực đông đúc này và nổ súng bừa bãi vào người dân cũng như các phương tiện xung quanh. Các đoạn video từ nhân chứng ghi lại cảnh người qua đường hoảng loạn tìm nơi trú ẩn khi tiếng súng vang lên và xe cứu thương nhanh chóng có mặt tại hiện trường.

Cơ quan cảnh sát xác định nghi phạm là một công dân Ba Lan 25 tuổi. Kẻ tấn công đã bị lực lượng an ninh bắn bị thương trong cuộc đấu súng gần đó và nhanh chóng được đưa đi cấp cứu tại bệnh viện. Bộ trưởng Nội vụ Ba Lan cho biết nghi phạm có xu hướng cực đoan và mang tư tưởng cực hữu, trong khi Bộ trưởng Quốc phòng gọi vụ tấn công này là một hành động khủng bố nhằm vào người dân thành phố.

Thống kê chính thức cho thấy vụ tấn công đã khiến sáu người thiệt mạng, bao gồm bốn phụ nữ và hai nam giới, trong đó có một công dân Anh. Ngoài ra, khoảng 16 người khác đã bị thương, bao gồm hai cảnh sát tham gia trấn áp trong đó có một người bị thương nặng. Các nhà chức trách cũng ghi nhận nhiều người nước ngoài khác từ Anh, Áo, Đức, Bồ Đào Nha và Nga nằm trong số những người bị thương.

Quá trình điều tra sau đó tiếp tục mở rộng khi Thủ tướng Ba Lan thông báo lực lượng chức năng phát hiện thêm ba thi thể tại nơi ở của nghi phạm, được cho là các thành viên trong gia đình. Sự việc chấn động này đã khiến chính phủ Ba Lan tuyên bố sẽ tổ chức quốc tang để tưởng niệm các nạn nhân, đồng thời các cơ quan chức năng đang tiếp tục làm rõ toàn bộ động cơ và quá trình chuẩn bị của kẻ tấn công.

article.title: Charlie Savage ghi bàn vào lưới đội bóng của cha tại FA Cup
article.summary: Trong khuôn khổ vòng một FA Cup, Charlie Savage đã trực tiếp ghi bàn giúp Reading giành chiến thắng đậm 5-0 trước Peterborough United, đội bóng đang được dẫn dắt bởi cha anh, ông Robbie Savage.
body: Vòng một FA Cup đã chứng kiến một khoảnh khắc đặc biệt khi Charlie Savage ghi bàn vào lưới Peterborough United, đội bóng hiện được dẫn dắt bởi cha anh, cựu cầu thủ Robbie Savage. Trận đấu diễn ra tại sân vận động Weston Homes, nơi Reading đã có màn trình diễn áp đảo để giành chiến thắng chung cuộc 5-0 và tiến vào vòng hai.

Reading sớm thiết lập thế trận vượt trội với các bàn thắng của Daniel Kyerewaa và Jack Marriott trong hiệp một. Ngay trước khi bước vào giờ nghỉ, Charlie Savage đã tận dụng cơ hội từ tình huống bóng bật ra để thực hiện cú sút chệch hướng, đưa bóng vào góc cao khung thành, nâng tỷ số lên 3-0 và làm sâu sắc thêm khó khăn cho đội bóng của cha mình. Trong hiệp hai, Jamie Reid ghi thêm hai bàn thắng nữa để ấn định chiến thắng đậm đà cho đội khách.

Sau trận đấu, hình ảnh Robbie Savage bắt tay con trai Charlie đã thu hút sự chú ý của người hâm mộ. Đối với Peterborough, đây là một thất bại nặng nề trong ngày thi đấu mà họ hoàn toàn bị đối thủ kiểm soát. Trong khi đó, Reading tiếp tục hành trình tại giải đấu lâu đời nhất nước Anh với sự tự tin cao độ sau màn trình diễn thuyết phục này.

article.title: Cơ hội nào cho Oregon Ducks nuôi mộng dự vòng play-off bóng bầu dục đại học?
article.summary: Sau chiến thắng quan trọng trước Ohio State, Oregon Ducks vẫn còn cơ hội mong manh để giành vé tham dự vòng play-off bóng bầu dục đại học (CFP) trong một mùa giải đầy biến động.
body: Mùa giải bóng bầu dục đại học năm 2026 chứng kiến những diễn biến bất ngờ đối với đội bóng Oregon Ducks. Dù phải trải qua ba trận thua từ đầu mùa, cùng với việc tiền vệ chính chấn thương dài hạn và sự thay đổi ở vị trí điều phối viên phòng ngự, đội bóng dưới sự dẫn dắt của huấn luyện viên Dan Lanning vẫn thắp lại hy vọng lọt vào vòng play-off nhờ chiến thắng thuyết phục 41-28 trước Ohio State.

Trong kỷ nguyên 12 đội của vòng play-off bóng bầu dục đại học, việc để thua ba trận thường được xem là bất lợi lớn đối với bất kỳ ứng viên nào. Lịch sử giải đấu ghi nhận chưa từng có đội bóng nào giành quyền vào vòng trong với ba thất bại. Do đó, việc lựa chọn suất đi tiếp theo diện vớt (at-large) tỏ ra vô cùng khó khăn đối với Oregon, khi thành tích đối đầu và danh sách các trận thắng lớn của họ còn khá khiêm tốn.

Tuy nhiên, con đường trực tiếp nhất để đội bóng giành vé tham dự vòng play-off là lọt vào trận chung kết hội nghị Big Ten, nơi nhà vô địch các giải đấu lớn sẽ nhận được suất vào thẳng. Hiện tại, Oregon đang nắm giữ thành tích 4 trận thắng và 2 trận thua tại đấu trường hội nghị. Nếu duy trì chuỗi thắng trong phần còn lại của mùa giải, họ có thể cải thiện thành tích lên 7 trận thắng và 2 trận thua.

Lịch thi đấu giai đoạn cuối của đội bóng được đánh giá là khá thuận lợi khi họ không phải đối mặt với thêm đối thủ nào đang nằm trong nhóm xếp hạng cao, trong đó cuộc đối đầu với Michigan được xem là thử thách đáng chú ý nhất. Dù vậy, để đạt mục tiêu giành vé trực tiếp, đội bóng không chỉ cần toàn thắng trong các trận đấu còn lại mà còn phải trông chờ vào kết quả bất lợi từ các đối thủ cạnh tranh trực tiếp tại bảng xếp hạng hội nghị Big Ten.

Gunman opens fire in Polish city of Krakow, killing 6 people and injuring 15 : NPRAccessibility links
Gunman opens fire in Polish city of Krakow, killing 6 people and injuring 15A gunman targeted random people as he drove into Krakow's Main Square, a major tourist spot. Police shot and wounded the gunman during a gunfight.
Gunman opens fire in Polish city of Krakow, killing 6 people and injuring 15
Police cars are parked in a cordoned off area after a shooter opened fire in a market square in Krakow, Poland, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026,Beata Zawrzel/APhide caption
KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — Six people were killed and 15 wounded after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a busy market square in Krakow,Poland, authorities said.
The gunman, a 24-year-old Polish citizen, aimed at random people as he drove into the Main Square, a major tourist destination inthe center of the city, Krakow police said. Four women and two men were killed. Two police officers were wounded, one seriously, Poland's interior minister said on X.
The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a gunfight with officers a short distance away from the initial violence, police said, and was taken to the hospital for surgery. The death toll earlier stood at five, but police updated it to six in a post on X.
Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, said the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said.
The attacker engaged in a "wild ride" around the Main Square, Cisło said, which is why people were wounded at several locations. Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby.
Cisło added that the gunman acted alone and that the public is safe.
It was not immediately clear whether the firearm used in Saturday's attack, or the guns found in the perpetrator's car, were legal. Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising.
Mass shootingsare uncommon in Poland. However, in mid-Octoberthree attacks at schoolsin the central province of Mazovia took placewithin four days, leaving one person dead and many wounded, including children.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a post on X, praised the police officers who responded to Saturday's tragedy. Polish President Karol Nawrocki said his thoughts were with the victims, the wounded and their families.
Images from the scene showed police officers and ambulances covering the area, and a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter also landed in the square.
A tram driver reported around 3 p.m. that his vehicle was shot at from a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The window to the tram driver's cabin was shattered.
Around15 million tourists a year visit Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, the majority passing through the Main Square.

Six dead after gunman opens fire in Kraków market square, with three more victims found at suspect’s home
Suspect was influenced by far-right ideology and held ‘ultra-nationalistic’ views, says Polish interior minister
Six people have been killed and 16 wounded after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Kraków, authorities said, in what Poland’s defence minister called an “act of terror” on the people of the city.
The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, opened fire with an automatic weapon in the city’s main square at about 3pm on Saturday.
He was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical” and “ultra-nationalistic” views, the Polish interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, said at a news conference.
View image in fullscreenEmergency personnel work at the site of the vehicle used in a shooting near the main market square of Krakow, Poland, 7 November 2026.Photograph: Jakub Porzycki/Reuters
Four women and two men were killed, one of them a British citizen, Polish police said. Three of the victims were Polish women and the remaining two victims had not been identified.
The foreign nationals wounded were from Britain, Austria, Germany, Portugal and Russia, a Polish government spokesperson said.
The ⁠injured included two police ⁠officers, one of whom is in a serious condition after being shot three times in the exchange of fire with the alleged attacker.
Late on Saturday night, Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, said two more women and one man had also been found dead in the suspect’s home, most likely members of his family, he added.
Five killed in Krakow market square shooting
The Polish defense minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, called Saturday’s fatal shooting an “act of terror” on the people of Krakow, Poland’s second-largest city, which receives 15 million visitors a year, most of them passing through the main square.
A tram driver reported about 3pm that his vehicle was shot at from a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The window to the tram driver’s cabin was shattered.
On Saturday evening, government spokesperson Adam Szłapka wrote on X: “Today’s event in Kraków has shaken all of Poland,” adding that Tusk was “on his way to Kraków”
View image in fullscreenEmergency personnel at the site of the shooting in Kraków.Photograph: Jakub Porzycki/Reuters
The justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, wrote on X that authorities would “ensure that the perpetrator of this crime is held fully accountable and severely punished”.
The Polish president, Karol Nawrocki, said he was “deeply concerned by reports of the tragic events” in Kraków, and that his thoughts are with victims, those injured and their families.
Earlier this year,Euronews reportedthat the number of legally owned firearms in Poland surpassed 1m for the first time.
Poland issued a record 50,700 gun permits in 2025, and the number of active permits registered in 2025 was almost double the number registered in 2015, according to the police statistics cited in the report.
Sunday and Monday will be a period of national mourning for the victims of the attack.

More than 230 fire and emergency medical personnel responded (file photo)
Six people have died after a large fire broke out in a residential building in Brooklyn, New York City, officials say.
Several others were hurt in the blaze, which occurred early on Thursday morning, the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) said in a statement.
More than 230 fire and emergency medical personnel were sent to the scene near Sunset Park after the fire was first reported at around 01:40 local time (06:40 GMT).
Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was "heartbroken" by the deaths, and has asked New Yorkers to "take a moment to pray for the full recovery of those who were injured".
The cause of the blaze is being investigated.
A crew specialising in hazardous materials was sent to the scene because of the presence of a lithium-ion battery, although it was not clear whether this was linked to the blaze.
The emergency responders reportedly discovered on their arrival that the building's first and second floors had been engulfed by flames.
Four individuals were pronounced dead at the scene, according to the FDNY.
A male and female were also taken to the hospital, where they were pronounced dead, the New York City Police Department (NYPD) said.
Six other civilians were injured, two of them critically, along with three firefighters, the FDNY said.

FA Cup roundup: Charlie Savage gets one over dad Robbie as Reading thrash Peterborough
Non-league Kidderminster stun Doncaster
Exeter upset Huddersfield in first round
Charlie Savage scored against his father’s team asReadingeased into the second round of the FA Cup with a 5-0 rout ofPeterboroughat the Weston Homes Stadium.
This all-League One tie turned out to be one of the most one-sided of the day, with the Peterborough manager, Robbie Savage, watching on in disbelief as his side were pulled apart.
Reading went ahead after 26 minutes as slick passing led to Andy Rinomhota playing in Daniel Kyerewaa, who found the bottom corner via a deflection.Readingdoubled their lead in the 34th minute when a cross from Haydon Roberts was met by a diving header from top scorer Jack Marriott.
It was in effect game over in first-half stoppage time as Savage deepened his father’s misery when he took possession after the ball ran off Marriott, his deflected effort finding the top corner.
Jamie Reid added a fourth for the visitors in the 72nd minute when Paudie O’Connor nodded Savage’s free-kick into his path for him to lift over the Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass. Reading struck yet again four minutes later when Liam Fraser’s pass put Reid clean through to score his second.
Non-leagueKidderminsterbreezed into the second round with a convincing 3-0 victory over League OneDoncaster.
The National League club opened the scoring after 22 minutes when Maz Kouhyar pulled the ball back to Lewis Walker, and he fired home at the second attempt after his initial shot had hit the upright.
View image in fullscreenDavid Davis celebrates a goal in Kidderminster’s FA Cup upset victory.Photograph: Matty Paddock
The Harriers striker continued to cause problems, putting an effort over the bar and another just wide, but in the 36th minute he turned provider, charging upfield before teeing up Kouhyar and the on-loanNotts Countymidfielder slotted home.
Doncaster had calls for a penalty waved away when Alfie May went sprawling on the deck as he tried to connect with a Jordan Thomas pass inside the area, but two minutes later they fell further behind. Kouhyar was again involved, having a shot that Josh Clarke could only parry and David Davis turned in the rebound.
The Kidderminster manager, Paul Wotton, said: “We started well, scored the goal and got the crowd up. It was just a really good day. They are a League One team at the end of the day, no matter what the scoreline suggests. They are two leagues higher than us, so they are going to have moments in the game, but we stood up to it.
“We’ve been playing well but just not getting our rewards. Today we got our rewards. It’s been a really good day for the football club and a really good day for the fans, which is what it’s all about – you could just see the atmosphere at the end.”
League TwoExeterpulled off an upset with a 2-1 win away to League One leadersHuddersfield. Exeter took the lead after 12 minutes, thanks to a perfectly delivered cross from the left from Luca Woodhouse, with centre-back Jack Taylor stealing in at the far post to finish it off.
Huddersfield looked a different team in the second half and found an equaliser within eight minutes of the restart as Ibane Bowat headed home Cameron Humphreys’ corner at the back post.
Charlie Cummins grabbed the winner nine minutes from time at the end of a well-worked move up the right, culminating in Reece Cole’s cutback and a good finish.
View image in fullscreenExeter’s Charlie Cummins celebrates after his late winner against Huddersfield.Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock
Blackpoolsurvived a scare atHornchurch, needing to rely on a 118th-minute winner from Josh Bowler to secure a 2-1 comeback victory at the Hornchurch Stadium.
Bowler, a half-time substitute, proved to be the gamechanger for Ian Evatt’s side, using his pace and trickery to alter the course of the tie.
Blackpool’s timidity in the first half allowed their National League opponents to claim a deserved half-time lead. Minutes after Josh Walker had shot straight at Blackpool keeper Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Ángelo Balanta then showed greater composure as the visiting defence was opened up again. Balanta slid in a clever cross that was stroked home by early Hornchurch substitute Henry Hearn.
Showing greater urgency in the second half, it was Bowler’s cross following a corner that was met by a sweetly struck Jordan Brown volley in the 55th minute to make it 1-1. The home side were then reduced to 10 men in the second period when Henry Sandat pulled back Bowler, who was bursting clear. From the resulting free-kick, Finley Munroe struck the Hornchurch bar.
And Blackpool’s pressure finally told when Tom Bloxham laid the ball in front of Bowler to curl home the late winner.
Altrinchamwere denied another famous FA Cup upset as they conceded an 84-minute equaliser againstNotts Countybefore bowing out in a penalty shootout.
County took the lead through Jacob Bedeau in the 28th minute but Altrincham responded well with Lucas Weaver grabbing an equaliser six minutes before half-time. Lewis Banks gave the hosts the lead just before the hour but Callum Roberts dashed Altrincham’s hopes of another cup scalp, having beaten 17 Football League sides in the competition, scoring with a first-time strike to force extra-time.
With neither side able to make a breakthrough in extra-time the game went to penalties and Aidan Barlow, Sam Taylor and Eddy Jones all missed from the spot for Altrincham as County triumphed 3-2.
Fleetwood’s hopes of following up their memorable Carabao Cup upset against Premier League champions Arsenal with a long FA Cup run are over after a 2-1 home defeat by fellow League Two sideRochdale. Baba Adeeko’s goal in extra time at Highbury sent the visitors through.
Chesterfieldwithstood a second-half comeback fromYeovil Townto secure their place in the second round with a 4-3 victory. Yeovil recovered from 3-1 down to level at 3-3 before Joel Randall struck the winner a minute from time.

Can Oregon make the CFP? Charting Ducks' path to playoff in season that once seemed lost | Sporting NewsSkip to main content
Can Oregon make the CFP? Charting Ducks' path to playoff in season that once seemed lost
If Oregon is going to be a College Football Playoff team in 2026, it would be arguably the wildest path to the bracket ever seen.
The Ducks — who have already endured three losses, their starting quarterback going down with a long-term injury and a change at defensive coordinator — got their biggest win of the season on Saturday, toppling Ohio State 41-28. Entering 2026, the Week 10 game was anticipated to have significant CFP consequences. While that was the case, those consequences look far different than one would have originally thought.
Thanks to a 41-point outing on Saturday, somehow, Oregon's path to the playoff isn't quite dead yet. It will take some help, but the Ducks will be looking to make CFP history over the next few weeks.
Here's a look at how Oregon can still make the CFP after upsetting Ohio State.
MORE:Bret Bielema rails against CFP committee in latest chapter of Big Ten-SEC feud
In the 12-team era of the CFP, a third loss has mostly been viewed as a death sentence for playoff contenders. No team has made the bracket with three losses, though it's not considered impossible. In the final rankings of a season, the highest a three-loss team has ranked was Alabama at No. 11 in 2025, but the Crimson Tide were still snubbed from the bracket.
Considering Oregon's only "resume" wins would be beating USC on the road, Boise State at home and an Ohio State team without Julian Sayin in Columbus, it's unlikely that the Ducks can make the bracket as an at-large selection. In 2024, the three-loss Alabama team had wins over No. 2 Georgia, No. 21 Missouri and No. 15 LSU, and still barely missed the playoff.
However, if Oregon can make the Big Ten title game, that would be a win-and-in scenario, as the Power 4 conference champions get an automatic berth to the CFP.
After Saturday's win, Oregon has a 4-2 record in Big Ten action. Assuming the Ducks win out, that number could improve to 7-2. But it would still take a bit of help for Dan Lanning's squad to reach the Big Ten Championship.
The following teams are either still ahead of or tied with Oregon in the Big Ten standings, with their updated conference records included:
Iowa (3-2) and Northwestern (3-2) will also face off on Saturday night.
The good news for Oregon isn't just that it has a favorable remaining schedule — the Ducks' wins over Ohio State and USC could come in handy for tiebreaker purposes. Even if Oregon finishes with the same conference record as either of those teams, the Ducks would get the nod thanks to their head-to-head win.
Illinois can at least be considered unlikely to reach the conference championship as well. The Illini face the unbeaten UCLA Bruins next week, then two more competitive Big Ten squads in Iowa and Northwestern.
That leaves Indiana as Oregon's likely biggest threat to reach the Big Ten Championship. The Hoosiers face No. 20 USC next week, a game Ducks fans should be rooting for the Trojans in. The second tiebreaker for Big Ten standings is record vs. common opponents — Oregon will be hoping that if Indiana loses to USC, the Hoosiers then either lose another game (vs. Washington and Purdue) or have a worse record against common opponents.
You can consider it unlikely that Oregon scrapes its way into the CFP, even if it wins out. But it's not impossible. The Ducks would at least need Indiana to falter, if not more added help, to reach a win-and-in scenario in the Big Ten Championship.

— Trojan Football ✌️ ᶠᵃⁿ (@TrojanFBx)November 7, 2026

The Ducks' path to a 9-3 season — and 7-2 conference record — is fairly straightforward. They do not face any more ranked teams, with Michigan in Week 11 being the toughest opponent.
All three of Oregon's remaining opponents have a losing record in Big Ten play. The question for the Ducks' playoff hopes will likely come down to other teams' results, including Indiana, Ohio State and USC.

NWSL playoff predictions: who can spoil Gotham’s bid for the double? | NWSL | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Rose Lavelle (Gotham), Croix Bethune (Kansas City) and Trinity Rodman (Washington) are among the stars seeking to lead their team to an NWSL title.Composite: Photo by Elsa/NWSL via Getty Images; Lachlan Cunningham/NWSL via Getty Images; Greg Fiume/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRose Lavelle (Gotham), Croix Bethune (Kansas City) and Trinity Rodman (Washington) are among the stars seeking to lead their team to an NWSL title.Composite: Photo by Elsa/NWSL via Getty Images; Lachlan Cunningham/NWSL via Getty Images; Greg Fiume/Getty Images
NWSL playoff predictions: who can spoil Gotham’s bid for the double?
Our panel breaks down the players to watch, the dark horses, the state of the league and the top candidates to reach the championship game in DC
Compelling storylines that kept the league interesting during a crowded sports summer.The interval years that aren’t Olympic or World Cup years are often quieter for the NWSL (see: average attendance wasessentially flatamong the non-expansion teams). In a year with the men’s World Cup on home soil and a major anniversary season for the WNBA, most of the NWSL’s teams gave a solid showing, with close competition for the Shield, an entertaining Golden Boot race and the returns of several big stars. Even those teams who didnotgive a solid showing – hello, Chicago – finally madesome encouraging movesin the right direction. (Louisville next, please.)Ella Brockway
The leagueworking to gauge the heart of its fanbase.Recent weeks have seen contentious scenes, especially in Portland, as transphobic organizations try to work into the league discourseas they havewith the WNBA. But beyond that, there have been considerable innovations made with an eye on garnering more attention. The“Rodman Rule”was hurried to production in part to keep arguably the most marketable US player from going abroad. The leaguebriefly considered following MLS’s leadand inverting its schedule, only for a vote to be spurned after initial backlash from players and the public. It even got a feature in Ted Lasso. These efforts take time, but that’s a lot of willingness to change just about anything about the league’s structure if it moves the needle.Jeff Rueter
Races to the top – and the bottom.The competition for both the Shield and Golden Boot was fierce. Ashley Sanchez pulled ahead for the Boot, but Barbra Banda, Sophia Wilson, Janine Sonis and Trinity Rodman provided some real fireworks. (Had Banda not been kept out of the country for the last month of games due to federal travel policies, she may have given Sanchez a run for her money.) The Shield race was even tighter, with three teams still in contention with two matches to go. However, the league struggled to maintain that quality across the board. Chicago, Louisville and Bay FC were embarrassingly bad – and boring – throughout the season. It’s a story that is too familiar, and doesn’t seem poised to change in a real way any time soon. As much as the league’s marketing centers parity, its choices prioritize expansion. With two new clubs arriving in 2028 and more on the way after, I worry the talent across the board will continue to be watered down, especially as the league’s salary cap and low minimum salary drives elite players away to teams in Europe, Mexico and Brazil. TheNWSLwill have to contend with what growing pains are inevitable, and which should really be avoided.Abigail Segel
Goals, guests and 6,561 scenarios: inside ESPN on the biggest NWSL Decision Day yetRead more
Best team that didn’t make the playoffs
Denver Summit.I’m as disappointed as anyone that we won’t get to see Sanchez’s goalscoring feats continue this postseason, but I’d also like to see what Denver and their goalscorers could have done as just the second expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in their first year. They tied 2018 North Carolina with the third-most goals (53) of a team in any regular season.EB
On talent and in moments, it felt like expansionDenver Summit’s place in the top eight would be inevitable. Ultimately, inconsistency and an inability to turn close games from draws into wins held them back. Only Chicago had a more languid defensive press after the summer break, and while being the league’s lowest-fouling team wins spirit points, it did afford Denver’s opponents plenty of time to build into sequences.JR
For the second year in a row, the North Carolina Courage.The Courage spent most of the season above the playoff line, but when Sanchez’s numbers came back down to earth in the final month, they lacked an attacking structure to keep the goalscoring, which had papered over their leaky defense all year. Mak Lind will look to use his first full offseason to find a sustainable way to make up for Manaka Matsukubo’s absence – her midseasondepartureto Chelsea did him no favors, and the success they had for almost the entire rest of the season is all the more impressive considering it.AS
View image in fullscreenAngel City, who haven’t lost since August, are our consensus dark-horse pick these playoffs.Photograph: Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images
Angel City.No team is in better form. After a rough start to the season, Angel City steadied the ship after the summer break and have been blistering of late, with eight wins, two draws and zero losses since 31 August. They have nine goals in their last three, and will have new signing Maddie DiMaria, fresh off a 12-goal showing at theU-17 World Cup, available to face Kansas City. I’d fear them.EB
For once, Gotham don’t qualify. SincesellingAlyssa Thompson to Chelsea,Angel Cityhave come out of their doldrums with impressive aptitude. No team has maintained a higher points-per-game rate since 28 August (2.6), and they notched a draw at Gotham and an away win over Washington. Ally Sentnor has made a quick acclimation, and there’s considerable talent including Sveindís Jónsdóttir’s goal threat, Emily Sams’s defensive mettle and Gisele Thompson’s all-around strengths.JR
Angel City.The club whose branding has traditionally been better than its soccer started the season hot, but within a few games they fell back to their expected place in the middle of the table. In June, GM Mark Parsons had seen enough, and gave the boot to manager Alexander Straus. His interim replacement, Leif Smerud, has managed to get the most out of the roster by bringing them back to the basics. E

Liên Quân Mobile 2026 có nhà vô địch mới
Tối 7-11 tại sân Mỹ Đình, Hà Nội, loạt chung kết Liên Quân Mobile 2026 - Đấu Trường Danh Vọng Mùa Đông đã diễn ra với cuộc thư hùng của các đội tuyển xuất sắc nhất.
FPT Polytechnic đăng quang ngôi vô địch - Ảnh: CAO THỦ LIÊN QUÂN
FPT Polytechnic và BOOM Esports là 2 đội cuối cùng bước vào tranh tài tại phần thi chung kết tổng, diễn ra khuya 7-11.
Dù bị đối thủ dẫn trước 1-2, FPT Polytechnic vẫn cho thấy bản lĩnh và phong độ ấn tượng khi liên tiếp giành chiến thắng trong 3 ván đấu cuối cùng để thắng ngược dòng với tỉ số 4-2.
Nhờ đó, FPT Polytechnic đăng quang ngôi vô địchĐấu Trường Danh Vọng Mùa Đông2026. Đây là dấu mốc đáng tự hào, tiếp tục khẳng định vị thế đang lên của FPT Polytechnic trên đấu trườngthể thao điện tử chuyên nghiệp quốc gia.
Đội hình FPT Polytechnic thi đấu gồm các game thủ: Nguyễn Thành Duy, Nguyễn Quang Duy, Lê Văn Việt, Đỗ Mạnh Hùng và Nguyễn Thế Khang. Chức vô địch này giúp đội nhận 1 tỉ đồng tiền thưởng theo thứ hạng, chưa bao gồm các khoản thưởng bonus.
Trước đó, tại vòng Playoffs, FPT Polytechnic thắng sát nút 4-2 Saigon Phantom để tiến vào chung kết nhánh thắng. Trong khi đó, BOOM Esports đánh bại SGP với tỉ số 4-2 ở chung kết nhánh thua.
ỞĐấu Trường Danh Vọng Mùa Đôngmùa giải trước, đội FPT Polytechnic chỉ đứng thứ 7. Nhà vô địch 2025 là đội FPT x Flash.
Sự kiện trên nằm trong chuỗi hoạt động kỷ niệm 10 năm của tựa game Liên Quân Mobile - Thập niên gắn kết, tổ chức trong 2 ngày 7 đến 8-11 tại sân vận động quốc gia Mỹ Đình.
Xác định nhà vô địch Cúp thể thao điện tử quốc gia 2026
Sự kiện thu hút đông đảo người hâm mộ đến tham dự, theo dõi các phần thi esports và trải nghiệm các hoạt động tương tác.
Ngày 8-11, chương trình tiếp tục với đại nhạc hội Liên Quân 10 Fest. Sự kiện có sự tham gia của hơn 30 nghệ sĩ, trong đó có Bích Phương, SOOBIN, Quang Hùng MasterD, Phùng Khánh Linh vàDa LAB.
Thái Lan khởi kiện VĐV Liên quân Mobile gian lận ở SEA Games 33
Liên quan vụ Tokyogurl, VĐV tuyển e-sports nữ Thái Lan tại SEA Games 33, bị phát hiện gian lận ở Liên quân Mobile (RoV), Thái Lan đã có động thái cứng rắn.

Lượt trận thứ tám - chặng 4 giảibilliardsđồng đội PBA Team League 2026-2027 tranh tài ngày 7.11. Trận đấu muộn nhất là màn so tài giữa đội Legend (cóNgô Đình Nại) và SY Builders. Ở trận này, Ngô Đình Nại cùng các đồng đội đã tạo ra màn lội ngược dòng ấn tượng và giành chiến thắng chung cuộc với tỷ số 4-2.
Ngô Đình Nại, Nguyễn Trần Thanh Tạo cùng thắng 11/1
Trước đó, đội Legend đã ra quân thuận lợi khi thắng ván đấu đôi nam. Nhưng đến ván đấu thứ hai và thứ ba (lần lượt đấu đôi nữ và đơn nam chạm 15 điểm), Legend lại liên tiếp để thua.
Khi đang bị dẫn trước 2-1, Legend đã bùng nổ trở lại và giành chiến thắng trong 3 ván đấu tiếp theo. Trong đó, Ngô Đình Nại xuất trận ở ván thứ năm (đấu đơn nam chạm 11 điểm). Cơ thủ Việt Nam đã giành chiến thắng đầy thuyết phục trước Yusuke Mori - VĐV người Nhật Bản từng giành chức vô địch PBA Tour.
Ngô Đình Nại vẫn đang miệt mài đi tìm chức vô địch PBA Tour (cá nhân) đầu tiên trong sự nghiệp
Ngay trong lượt cơ đầu tiên, Đình Nại đã có sê-ri 6 điểm. Đây chính là tiền đề cho đại diện Việt Nam đánh bại Mori với điểm số cách biệt 11/1, sau 4 lượt cơ.
Chiến thắng này giúp Legend giữ vững ngôi đầu trên bảng xếp hạng của chặng 4 PBA Team League mùa này. Đội của Ngô Đình Nại hiện có 18 điểm (6 thắng, 2 thua).
Cùng ngày, đội Welcome Phoenix thắng nghẹt thở với tỷ số 4-3 trước Weebies. Trong đó, Nguyễn Trần Thanh Tạo là người đã ấn định chiến thắng cho tập thể "phượng hoàng". Trước đó, khi trận đấu đang ở thế cân bằng với tỷ số 3-3, Thanh Tạo xuất trận ở ván cuối cùng (đấu đơn nam chạm 11 điểm), so tài cao thủ Hàn Quốc Kang Min-gu.
Thanh Tạo chỉ mất vỏn vẹn 2 lượt cơ để đánh bại gương mặt từng lên ngôi vô địch PBA Tour. Đại diện Việt Nam đề-pa ghi 2 điểm. Sau đó, tay cơ sinh năm 1997 tiếp tục tung sê-ri 9 điểm để thắng cách biệt 11/1 trước Kang Min-gu.
Kết quả các cặp đấu còn lại thuộc lượt trận thứ tám vào ngày 7.11: Laon 4-3 Breakers, NH Pay 4-0 Harim, Hana Card 4-3 High1 Winners.
