Khán giả Việt Nam Xanh 'giành' hát với Negav, Nguyễn Phi Hùng quá cháy
và 4 tác giả khácLAN HƯƠNGHY THÀNHMAI NGUYỆTMỸ HIỀNVY THANH
Đêm nhạc khuấy động không khí ngày hội Việt Nam Xanh với sự góp mặt của Negav cùng nhiều nghệ sĩ, mang đến màn trình diễn sôi động, lan tỏa thông điệp bảo vệ môi trường đến giới trẻ.
Negav đầy tinh nghịch, mang "kho tàng" hit đến Greeen Concert chiêu đãi người hâm mộ - Ảnh: QUANG ĐỊNH
Tối 7-11, đêm nhạc Green Concert trong khuôn khổNgày hội Việt Nam Xanh 2026diễn ra đầy sôi đội, rộn ràng tại công viên Phan Đình Phùng (123 Pasteur, phường Xuân Hòa, TP.HCM).
Ngay từ 16h, đông đảo khán giả đã có mặt tại khu vực sân khấu, háo hức xếp hàng, giữ chỗ để chờ đợi đêm nhạc diễn ra.

Tất cả sẵn sàng hòa mình vào những màn trình diễn bùng nổ, "cháy" hết mình cùng "anh trai"Negav, đắm chìm trong những giai điệu đầy cảm xúc qua giọng hát của Nguyễn Phi Hùng, Quốc Đại, Dương Quốc Hưng, Trung Hiếu...
Trước giờ G, không khí đêm nhạc đã dần trở nên sôi động với minigame cùng loạt phần quà hấp dẫn dành tặng khán giả.
Nổi bật trong số đó là xe điện VinFast trị giá 43 triệu đồng, túi mỹ phẩm Cocoon, sữa, nước giải khát cùng nhiều phần quà trải nghiệm thú vị khác.
Khán giả may mắn nhận giải thưởng trị giá 5 triệu đồng tại Green Concert - Ảnh: QUANG ĐỊNH
Chúng ta sẽ để lại gì cho thế hệ mai sau?
Mở đầu chương trình là ca khúcHành trình của lá, gửi gắm thông điệp về vòng đời tự nhiên, sự trưởng thành và giá trị của mỗi chiếc lá trong hệ sinh thái.
Đó cũng chính là tinh thần mà Ngày hội Việt Nam Xanh hướng đến, cùng lan tỏa ý thức sống xanh, gìn giữ thiên nhiên và xây dựng một tương laibền vững.
Xuất hiện tại đêm nhạc Green Concert,Hoa hậu Bảo Ngọcmở đầu phần giao lưu bằng câu hỏi gần gũi: "Bạn đến từ đâu?".
Câu hỏi nhanh chóng nhận được sự hưởng ứng nhiệt tình từ khán giả.
Hoa hậu Lê Nguyễn Bảo Ngọc nêu rõ tầm quan trọng khi người trẻ sở hữu kiến thức về lối sống xanh - Ảnh: QUANG ĐỊNH
Từ miền Bắc, miền Trung đến miền Nam, mỗi vùng miền đều có những câu chuyện, nhưng có một điểm chung là đều từng phải đối mặt với thiên tai và những tác động ngày càng rõ nét của biến đổi khí hậu.
Từ sự kết nối ấy, Bảo Ngọc khéo léo dẫn dắt khán giả cùng nhìn nhận những vấn đề môi trường đang hiện hữu và ý thức hơn về trách nhiệm chung trong hành trình bảo vệ hành tinh.
Hoa hậu, hoa khôi check-in rộn ràng Ngày hội Việt Nam Xanh 2026
Nàng hậu kể về câu chuyện về quốc đảo Fiji, Tuvalu - những nơi đang phải đối mặt với nguy cơ chịu ảnh hưởng nghiêm trọng từ nước biển dâng và biến đổi khí hậu.
Theo cô, đây không phải là câu chuyện của thế giới mà ngay cảViệt Namcũng đang phải đối mặt.
"Nếu như thế hệ chúng ta không hành động thì chúng ta sẽ để lại gì cho thế hệ mai sau?" - cô đặt câu hỏi.
Từ đó, Bảo Ngọc nhấn mạnh ý nghĩa của chuyển đổi xanh.
Theo nàng hậu, đây không đơn thuần là việc thay đổi một vài thói quen sinh hoạt.
Đó là sự chuyển đổi toàn diện trong cách con người phát triển kinh tế, sản xuất và vận hành xã hội, hướng đến mục tiêu phát triển bền vững, hài hòa với thiên nhiên.
Theo Bảo Ngọc, việc chủ động cập nhật kiến thức về biến đổi khí hậu, chính sách môi trường và phát triển bền vững sẽ là hành trang cần thiết cho mỗi người - Ảnh: QUANG ĐỊNH
Gửi gắm thông điệp đến các bạn trẻ, Bảo Ngọc cho rằng thế hệ trẻ không nên đứng ngoài câu chuyện chuyển đổi xanh.
"Bên cạnh việc học hỏi và đổi mới, tôi mong các bạn sẽ tiếp tục tham gia những hoạt động cộng đồng như Việt Nam Xanh ngày hôm nay.
Đôi khi, đóng góp cho môi trường không nhất thiết phải bắt đầu bằng những điều quá lớn lao.
Đó có thể là một buổi tình nguyện nhặt rác, một hoạt động tái chế hay đơn giản là chủ động tìm hiểu thêm về chính sách khí hậu và những vấn đề môi trường đang diễn ra xung quanh mình" - cô nói.
Là ca sĩ đầu tiên biểu diễn trong chương trình, ca sĩQuốc Đạimang đến ca khúcViệt Nam quê hương tôivàViệt Nam tinh hoa.
Xuất hiện trong tà áo dài xanh, nam ca sĩ thể hiện những giai điệu quen thuộc về quê hương, đất nước bằng chất giọng truyền cảm.
Cả hai ca khúc đều nhận được sự hưởng ứng của đông đảo khán giả.Đặc biệt, trong phần trình diễn, ca sĩ Quốc Đại bước xuống sân khấu, di chuyển dọc lối giữa khu vực fanzone và mời khán giả hát cùng.
Khán giả hào hứng giao lưu với ca sĩ Quốc Đại tại Green Concert - Ảnh: QUANG ĐỊNH
Sự tương tác gần gũi giữa nam ca sĩ và khán giả góp phần khuấy động không khí, mở màn sôi động cho đêm nhạc hội Green Concert.
Sự xuất hiện của ca sĩ Dương Quốc Hưng cùng màn hòa giọng với khán giả trong ca khúc Việt Nam trong tôi tiếp nối bầu không khí đầy hào hùng và tự hào dân tộc tại đêm nhạc.
Với ca khúcNgày mới trên thành phố, nam ca sĩ tiếp tục khuấy động sân khấu và mang đến nguồn năng lượng trẻ trung.
Ngay sau đó, Dương Quốc Hưng đưa khán giả đến với một màu sắc âm nhạc hoàn toàn khác qua ca khúcMột đêm say.

The 19 Best Early Black Friday Deals 2026 | WIREDSkip to main content
While the Fridayafter Thanksgiving has traditionally been the busiest shopping day of the year, Black Friday deals have gradually spread well beyond the day. First came Cyber Monday, then Cyber Week. Now, early Black Friday deals kick off before November has even started. The tricky part for early birds is knowing what’s a genuine deal and what’s likely to go even lower when Black Friday arrives.
TheReviews teamat WIRED tracks prices on our favorite gadgets year-round, and we only highlight deals on devices we've tested and would recommend to our own friends and family. Some of these picks may be cheaper for Black Friday, but these are the discounts that have caught our eye so far.
Updated November 7: We've added new deals on Google Pixel 11 phones, Google Pixel earbuds, a Rocco minifridge, a Dreo space heater, and a Petkit automatic litter box. We've also checked for accuracy throughout.Louryn Strampecontributed to this story.
Photograph: James D. Morgan/Getty Images
Thebest trackersfor anyone with an iPhone; you can use them to keep tabs on your keys, luggage, bike, or whatever else you worry might go missing. Each AirTag location is marked clearly in the Find My app. The battery should last you a year, and we have aguide on how to replace your AirTag battery. Just please don’t use themto track people. This is the lowest price we have seen on the single tag, but it drops this low pretty frequently.
For Apple fans with an iPhone or MacBook, theApple AirPods Max 2are the best over-ear headphones. They offer great sound quality, effective noise cancellation, and good transparency modes. They are usually a little too pricey for our tastes compared to Sony and Bose options, but at $100 off, they look more tempting. Before you pull the trigger, they will likely drop by at least another $30 for Black Friday.
If you want to pair wireless earbuds with your iPhone and enjoy a seamless, feature-rich experience, you should snag theAirPods Pro 3. They are comfy, boast top-notch active noise cancellation, and can even translate some languages in real time. That said, they are at this price often enough that I hesitate to call it a great deal, and they will likely drop by another $20 for Black Friday.
At $10 below their all-time lowest price, this is a great deal if you're in the market for ourtop Android earbuds. ThePixel Buds Pro 2are comfortable, have a long-lasting battery, and have clear sound with seamless noise cancellation. We think they're especially good for listeners with small ears. They might get cheaper for Black Friday or Cyber Monday, but likely not by much.
Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL
Google's full Pixel 11 lineup is on sale for less than we've seen all year long. Like some of these other tech deals, it's possible that we see prices drop a bit more later this month, but we don't anticipate it being by much. Each of these phones features incredible cameras and snappy performance, and they're available in a wide array of eye-catching colors. Whether you go with the baseGoogle Pixel 11or opt for the11 Pro or 11 Pro XL, you'll be getting one ofour favorite Android phones.
With a great camera, solid performance, and super-slick software features, thePixel 10 Prois an excellent Android phone. It also has proper Qi2 support for fast wireless charging, but more importantly, the magnets inside make it easy to attach to docks and chargers. Its bigger sibling, the Pro XL, has been my daily driver for most of the last year, and it has served me well. It has frequently dropped to this price before, but I still think it’s a good deal. Note that Amazon prices may vary based on the seller, so double check before adding to cart.
Photograph: Julian ChokkattuSave to wishlist
MagSafe 3-in-1 Extendable Wireless Charging Stand
This is one of ourfavorite 3-in-1 chargersfor keeping your iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch charged up from a single outlet. The unique feature is its height adjustability, enabling it to pull double duty as a tripod for shooting video or FaceTime calls with family or friends. It has been on sale (close to half price) for a while now but has never been lower than $60 at Best Buy. Snap it up while you still can.
Photograph: Simon HillSave to wishlist
Uno 2-in-1 Magnetic Wireless Charger
Gadgets are too boring. I want more anthropomorphized devices in my life. Ugreen simply added a wee robot face to this wireless charger that changes its expression based on the charging status. I immediately like it more than all my old faceless chargers. The charging pad supports Qi2/MagSafe and tilts up to 70 degrees to reveal a second pad to charge AirPods or other wireless earbuds. It even has a USB-C port for a third gadget. At 40 percent off, this is the lowest price I’ve seen.
My pick for thebest budget Wi-Fi routerdips down to this price fairly often, but it’s a great deal for a Wi-Fi 7 router with four antennas, a 2.5-Gbps WAN, a 2.5-Gbps LAN, and three gigabit LAN ports. It’s only dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), so there’s no 6-GHz option, and performance is limited, but for a small home with modest demands, this is a tough price to beat.
I always associate Black Friday with footage of excited shoppers struggling to carry huge TVs out of big box stores. The reality is that most Black Friday TV deals are on terrible models you should never buy. But this deal on LG’s 55-inch C6 OLED TV caught my eye. At $400 off the regular price, it is the cheapest it's ever been. The sale price on the 65-incher also makes it a better option than the entry-levelLG B6we just reviewed. Just make sure you pair it with a streaming device and disable the tracking.
This security camera records video at up to 2K at 30 frames per second, offers a 150-degree field of view, and connects directly to your Wi-Fi network. The Tapo app can detect motion (person, pet, vehicle) and enables you to set activity zones and privacy zones. The two-way audio is okay, and there’s a built-in alarm function. You can also slip a microSD card in for local recording. It lacks HDR, but it still earns a spot in ourbest outdoor security camerasguide. It has bounced between $90 and $65 for the last year, but it’s now down to $60.
It may not be one of thebest video doorbellsyou can buy, but at this sale price, Blink’s latest wired doorbell is the cheapest option worth considering. It delivers reasonably good 2K footage and passable two-way audio, tho

Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Au was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state"
ByKelly NgandAbel U,BBC Chinese,Reporting fromMacau
Macau has sentenced an ex-lawmaker and pro-democracy campaigner to 12 years and six months' jail in the city's first national security case.
Following a closed-door trial, Au Kam San, 69, was convicted on Friday of "subversion against the political power of the state", among other offences.
His wife Virginia Cheang condemned the ruling, calling the case a "groundless persecution designed to humiliate Au".
Macau was handed back to China in 1999, ending over 400 years of Portuguese administration. Its national security law came into effect in 2009, criminalising acts of treason, secession, and subversion against the Chinese Communist Party.
The law was revised in 2023, broadening its scope to include non-violent acts of secession, and again this year, to allow for trials to be held behind closed doors.
Prosecutors had accused Au of assisting and collaborating with "external hostile organisations" by collecting, preparing and disseminating information that was "manifestly filled with political claims of a subversive nature against the state".
These took place "over a long period of time", the prosecutors claim.
Au was arrested in July 2025 and later charged with three counts of subverting the state's power, three counts of endangering national security by establishing contact with foreign organisations, and one count of breach of confidentiality.
He was found guilty of four of the seven charges following a three-day trial which ended in September. A judge had ordered that the trial be held behind closed doors "to ensure that no prejudice is caused to the interests of national security".
Macau's authorities never publicly disclosed the details of the case. Au's family had earlier told the media Au was not allowed to seek his own legal representation and had instead been assigned a lawyer by the court.
Au's wife Cheang said she hoped authorities would grant her and her family permission to regularly write to and visit Au in prison.
"I dare not hope for more as I believe that will only lead to greater disappointment," she said in an open letter on Friday.
Au, who was formerly a primary school teacher, was elected to the Legislative Assembly in September 2001. For 20 years, he served as one of only a handful of pro-democracy lawmakers in the legislature, largely made up of pro-Beijing loyalists.
Au had co-organised annual vigils in Macau to commemorate the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing.
These vigils were previously tolerated in places like Macau and Hong Kong, but have effectively been banned in both cities since China imposed a sweeping national security law on Hong Kong in 2020.
Au's jailing comes a day after Hong Kong sentenced Joshua Wong, the face of its now-quashed democracy movement, to10 years in jail. Wong, 30, whose activism started when he was just a teen, has been in custody for the last six years.

Add Al Jazeera on GoogleLos Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman speaks at an election night event in Los Angeles, California, on November 3, 2026 [Jae C Hong/AP Photo]ByAl Jazeera StaffandThe Associated PressPublished On 5 Nov 20265 Nov 2026|Updated: 13 hours agoUpdated: 13 hours ago
Nithya Raman, a progressive Los Angeles City Council member, has defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass, putting her on track to become the first South Asian to lead the second-largest city in the United States.
The Associated Press news agency called the race for Raman on Thursday, with her holding 52 percent of the vote.

Raman, 45, overtook Bass despite endorsements for the incumbent from prominent Democrats such as California Governor Gavin Newsom, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi.
Raman’s campaign was backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), with her victory coming as part of a surge in visibility and electoral wins for the left-wing political movement.
Arecord numberof candidates backed by or affiliated with the DSA won federal offices in Tuesday’s midterm elections. On its website, the DSA has claimed credit for contributing to at least 300 candidacies or ballot referendums during the midterms, and it said it is on track to count 105 of those as victories.
Several of those wins came in congressional races, with figures such as Darializa Avila Chevalier, Claire Valdez, Melat Kiros and Chris Rabb winning their first terms as US representatives.
Raman’s victory in Los Angeles follows another high-profile democratic socialist winning a mayor’s race in New York City last year: Zohran Mamdani.
Raman and Mamdani are of Indian origin – and now lead the country’s two biggest cities.
But while Mamdani spent his early years in Uganda, Raman was born in India, in the southern state of Keralam.
She moved to the US with her family when she was six years old, but later returned to India, where she worked as an urban planner in the city of Chennai.
In 2013, she moved to Los Angeles, where she worked as an administrative officer in the city government before launching a nonprofit to tackle homelessness.
Once an ally of Bass, she had initially endorsed her re-election campaign but reversed course, entering the mayoral race in February, just hours before the filing deadline.
In her victory speech, Raman promised to restore what she called an ambitious, creative and entrepreneurial Los Angeles.
“For too long our broken and unjust status quo has convinced Angelenos that this is the best that we can do,” she told the crowd.
Raman also pledged to expand affordable housing, improve neglected city services and take a different approach to homelessness by deploying more medical teams to assist people who are unhoused.
In addition, she called for replacing the city’s police chief over concerns about cooperation with federal immigration authorities.
Raman now faces the task of delivering on those promises in a city of more than 3.8 million people.
Los Angeles also faces the challenge of hosting the 2028 Olympic Games, which open in July of that year.
With the result, Bass has become the first Los Angeles mayor in more than two decades to lose a re-election bid.
Her defeat follows a difficult four years in office. Her administration faced mounting criticism over the city’s homelessness crisis and its response to the deadlyPalisades Fire, which broke out while she was overseas and devastated communities across the Los Angeles area.
In a statement on Thursday, Bass congratulated Raman and said she was committed to ensuring a smooth transition.
“Four years ago, you elected me as the first Black woman mayor in the history of Los Angeles. You gave me the honor of serving the city that raised me, and every single day since, I have carried that responsibility with me,” Bass wrote.
“Moving this city forward is what Los Angeles needs from all of us.”

article.title: Phụ nữ U.35+ giảm cân cần tránh 3 cạm bẫy chuyển hóa phổ biến
article.summary: Bước sang tuổi 35, quá trình trao đổi chất thay đổi khiến việc giữ dáng gặp nhiều khó khăn. Nhận diện và tránh ba sai lầm về dinh dưỡng, tập luyện cùng giấc ngủ sẽ giúp phái đẹp lấy lại vóc dáng thon gọn.
body: Bước sang ngưỡng tuổi U.35+, nhiều phụ nữ nhận thấy cơ thể thay đổi rõ rệt khi các phương pháp nhịn ăn hay tập luyện thông thường không còn mang lại hiệu quả giảm mỡ như trước. Theo các chuyên gia, nguyên nhân chính bắt nguồn từ sự suy giảm tốc độ trao đổi chất cơ bản và những biến động nội tiết tố trong cơ thể.

Cạm bẫy đầu tiên là việc nhịn ăn gián đoạn hoặc cắt giảm calo quá mức. Khi năng lượng nạp vào sụt giảm đột ngột, cơ thể sẽ kích hoạt chế độ sinh tồn, làm chậm tốc độ đốt cháy calo và tăng sản xuất hormone cortisol gây tích mỡ nội tạng. Chuyên gia khuyến nghị thay vì nhịn ăn, phái đẹp nên tập trung vào mật độ dinh dưỡng, bổ sung protein chất lượng cao và áp dụng quy tắc đĩa ăn cân bằng gồm rau xanh, đạm và tinh bột phức.

Sai lầm thứ hai đến từ việc lạm dụng các bài tập cardio cường độ cao nhưng thiếu các bài tập kháng lực. Vận động quá sức ở độ tuổi này có thể làm tiêu hao khối lượng cơ bắp và gia tăng tình trạng viêm. Do đó, việc phân bổ thời gian hợp lý cho các bài tập tạ kết hợp rèn luyện nhóm cơ vùng lõi sẽ giúp siết chặt vòng eo hiệu quả hơn.

Yếu tố cuối cùng thường bị bỏ quên là giấc ngủ và sự suy giảm nội tiết tố. Thiếu ngủ mạn tính làm gia tăng hormone kích thích cảm giác thèm ăn và làm suy giảm độ nhạy insulin. Đảm bảo thời gian ngủ đủ giấc, đi ngủ sớm cùng việc bổ sung các vi chất hỗ trợ chuyển hóa là chìa khóa quan trọng giúp phái đẹp duy trì vóc dáng săn chắc.

lead_title: Alcaraz beats Fritz to help Jodar reach ATP finals

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/tennis/artic:
Paris Masters: Carlos Alcaraz saves two match points to beat Taylor Fritz in quarter-finals and help Rafael Jodar qualify for ATP finals - BBC Sport
Image source,EPA/ShutterstockImage caption,
Carlos Alcaraz is a seven-time Grand Slam winner
ByTimothy AbrahamBBC Sport Journalist
Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points to beat Taylor Fritz in the Paris Masters quarter-finals - a result which helped Spanish compatriot Rafael Jodar qualify for the ATP Finals.
Alcaraz claimed a 6-7 (10-12) 7-5 6-3 win over Fritz which also ended the American's hopes of reaching the season-ending event in Turin, Italy.
Fritz edged a tight opening set, winning the tie-break after both players had chances to take it.
He then moved a break ahead in the second set, but Alcaraz rallied to level the match after saving two match points and breaking his opponent twice.
The 23-year-old Spaniard dominated the decider after moving 3-1 ahead before closing out the contest with a powerful forehand.
"I tried not to let myself down in those difficult moments - to stay strong mentally," said Alcaraz, who will face either Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges in the semi-finals.
"We played incredible tennis, both of us, and I used the energy of the people to give them what they wanted to watch. To entertain them."
Alcaraz's victory secured 20-year-old Jodar's place at the finals, which will be held at Turin's Inalpi Arena from 15 to 22 November.
Earlier, Tommy Paul's hopes were dashed after he suffered a 6-4 4-6 6-3 defeat to fellow American Ben Shelton, which propelled Frances Tiafoe into the finals.
American Tiafoe, 28, and Spain's Jodar will both make their debuts at the event, which features the top eight men's singles players in the world.
The eight qualifiers are Alexander Zverev, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Alcaraz, Shelton, Tiafoe and Jodar.
Jodar only became a full-time professional at the beginning of 2026, but his debut season has drawn major attention and widespread excitement.
The Madrid-born youngster won three ATP Challenger titles in 2025 before he claimed his first ATP Tour title in Marrakech in April 2026.
Jodar,dubbed the new Rafa Nadal, also reached the quarter-finals of this year's French Open and climbed into the world's top 10 for the first time.
At 6ft 3in, he hits heavy, high-speed shots loaded with topspin from the baseline that are designed to force opponents into submission.
His serve is several miles per hour faster than the tour average and his attacking style means he is prone to taking risks on big points and in rallies.
Tiafoe, meanwhile, is a three-time ATP Tour title winner who reached a career-high ranking of 10th in the world in 2023.
He reached the US Open semi-finals in 2022 and 2024, knocking out Nadal en route to the last four in 2022.
He won his biggest title to date in Halle in 2026 and also reached the finals in Cincinnati and Acapulco.
The Maryland-born player, nicknamed 'Big Foe', is known for his energetic style and passionate celebrations.

Highlights from a thrilling quarter-final at the Paris Masters as Carlos Alcaraz fought from a set down to beat Taylor Fritz
Taylor Fritz missed out on claiming the last spot at the ATP Finals in Turin later this month after squandering two match points in his Paris Masters quarter-final defeat to Carlos Alcaraz.
Fritz would have reached the end-of-season event in Italy at Rafael Jodar's expense had he beaten Alcaraz to make the last four.
He looked poised to do that after twice finding himself a point from victory in the second set, once on his opponent's serve at 5-3 up and then on his own with the score at 5-4.
However, Alcaraz rallied during a high-quality match to triumph 6-7 (10-12) 7-5 6-3 and ensure he will be joined by compatriot Jodar at the ATP Finals from November 15-22, live onSky Sports.

Highlights from the Paris Masters as Ben Shelton advanced to the semi-finals and ended opponent Tommy Paul's hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals in Turin
Tommy Paul's three-set defeat to fellow American Ben Shelton earlier in the day - US Open finalist Shelton prevailing 6-4 4-6 6-3 - had ended his hopes of reaching the ATP Finals, with countryman Frances Tiafoe's place subsequently secured.
Fritz was looking to become the third US representative in this year's Turin showpiece, after Shelton and Tiafoe, but squandered a golden opportunity to get there and also defeat Alcaraz for just the second time in eight attempts.
Image:Fritz's heart-breaking defeat to Alcaraz confirmed Rafael Jodar's place in the ATP Finals later this month
The 29-year-old won the first set after a lengthy tie-break and then broke Alcaraz to open up a 4-3 lead in the second set, before saving a break point to make that 5-3.
Alcaraz had already qualified for the ATP Finals - an event he is yet to win in three previous tries - alongside world No 1 Alexander Zverev, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Shelton and Tiafoe.
Home hopes in Turin will rest on Cobolli, with Jannik Sinner -who on Friday announced a split with coach Darren Cahill after five years- ending his campaign early due to a knee problem that has sidelined him since winning Wimbledon in July.
Image:Spain's Rafael Jodar will make his ATP Finals debut in Turin
Alcaraz will face Casper Ruud in the semi-finals in Paris after the Norwegian saw off Portugal's Nuno Borges 7-6 (7-5) 6-4, with Shelton meeting home player Luca Van Assche, who overcame Australian qualifier - and Novak Djokovic's conqueror - Rinky Hijikata 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 7-5.
Should we get an Alcaraz-Shelton final in France, it would be a repeat of their five-set epic in the US Open quarter-finals, a match Shelton won in a final-set tie-break at Flushing Meadows.
Alcaraz said after fighting back against Fritz: "I tried not to let myself down in those difficult moments - to stay strong mentally.
"We played incredible tennis, both of us, and I used the energy of the people to give them what they wanted to watch. To entertain them."

From the front row to the hot seat — what the midterms mean for Big Tech
Dominic-Madori Davis8:16 PM PST · November 6, 2026
Right before the midterm elections, OpenAIhired Jessica Schumer, daughter of Democratic Sen. Chuck Schumer. The company also said it would start calling its data centers “compute campuses.”
For the past two years, many of Silicon Valley’s biggest names have built closer ties with President Donald Trump and his administration. Several attended White House events, some companies scaled back diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and some executives donated millions to super PACs supporting his campaign and allied candidates. Administration policies also benefited the industry, including tax breaks, the pausing of some federal investigations, and looser AI regulation. Meanwhile, Meta faced lawsuits and billion-dollar fines, and OpenAI faced suits alleging its technology harmed users.
Now, with the midterms shifting the balance of power in Washington, those same companies are working to rebuild ties with Democrats, who have pledged to tighten oversight of AI. How far that gets them may depend less on image-polishing than on where the real fights are happening: in state capitols, in communities deciding whether to host data centers, and, as we’ve seen this past week, in the markets watching the AI boom.
J.B. Branch, director of federal AI governance and technology policy at Public Citizen, a nonprofit advocacy group that describes itself as nonpartisan, told me that the tech industry “realizes they have an optics problem.” He characterized moves like the Schumer hire and the rebranding as “PR washing.” He expects more of it, too, pointing to OpenAI’s partnership with the American Federation of Teachers, announced last year, as well as Anthropic’s newly launched Claude Corps and Meta’s America’s Workforce Academy. “I would imagine more of that sort of investment in these corporate, private-public partnerships,” he said.
These initiatives didn’t spring up overnight. Meta and other tech companies reportedly began looking for ways to strengthen their ties to Democrats as Democratic gains in the midterms looked more likely. Reached for comment about the midterm elections’ impact on Meta, a company spokesperson pointed TechCrunch to remarks that Meta President Dina Powell McCormick made this week at WSJ Tech. “You have to work with the government that the American people elect,” McCormick had said. “I have seen it across the board that you have to be bipartisan, and you want to be, because you want buy-in on the things that you’re trying to do.”
Not everyone expects them to work. Alice Marwick, director of research at the tech policy nonprofit Data & Society, told me she expects Big Tech to try to pivot back toward the middle, “if not the left. But it’s a little too late,” she said. “Tech companies should be asking themselves how their products can make people’s lives better, because right now, it doesn’t seem like they are.”
If Democrats follow through on pledges to tighten oversight of AI and Big Tech, the industry could face a tougher environment. Data center moratoriums are gaining traction, and a wave of AI regulation bills awaits drafting. At the same event, Powell McCormick said Meta wants to show that communities welcoming its investments will see “an enormous amount of benefit,” while those that don’t want them “will of course have the right to stop them.”
Still, the next two years could bring political gridlock in Washington. Aryan Ranjan, founder of Baraza, a political campaign management software company, told me most action will likely happen at the state level, since states have already sued tech companies and passed regulations. “A coalition built on newer, working-class voters is likely to push Democrats to frame AI around electricity bills, data-center siting and jobs rather than abstract AI safety,” he said of what to expect at the federal level.
Last December, the Trump administration signed an executive order creating theAI Litigation Task Force, a federal group meant to challenge state AI laws. The administration has argued that U.S. AI companies “must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulations.” Many states have nonetheless passed their own laws, including measures on chatbots and deepfakes.
It also remains to be seen how President Trump will respond, including whether he’ll sign more AI executive orders or veto bills that could be seen as anti-AI. Clearly, voters wantstronger guardrailsaround the technology.
In a statement to TechCrunch, a White House official said: “American leadership in super intelligence is essential for our national security, economic prosperity, and the quality of life of the American people. President Trump is committed to ensuring America continues to lead the world in super intelligence while protecting American consumers. As the President has said, he’s willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.”
Branch argued that Trump’s political fortunes are now tied to the AI industry. On Wednesday, the day after the midterms, a trillion-dollar market sell-off spooked investors, some are whom are reportedly now reconsidering Anthropic’s reported trillion-dollar IPO. “There’s a very strong likelihood that there will be an AI bubble pop, and it’ll happen on Trump’s hands,” Branch said, predicting a possible market collapse. “Does he want to sink or swim along with the AI industry?”
For now, the rules companies face may vary by location. “For the next two years, a company’s AI rules may depend more on where it operates rather than on anything Washington passes,” Ranjan said.

Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta are on the hook with their data center plans.
Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty ImagesPart OfFall 2026 earnings watchsee allEllen Thomas
is an independent reporter focused on business investigations, analysis and news. She previously covered the AI data center boom for Business Insider.
After four of the biggest competitors in the AI race held quarterly earnings calls late last month, two things are clear: Big Tech is not done spending record amounts on the AI data center buildout, and the AI data center buildout is not any closer to yielding its promised returns.
A third thing is also starting to become clear — Big Tech will not be slowing down, at least not on its own.
The fight for tech accountability starts now
Not even $200 million could help Elon Musk buy Texas
Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta told investors they’re planning to spend at least $720 billion on CapEx this year alone. Most of that will go toward AI infrastructure. That’s on top of at least $1 trillion in spending commitments that have been arranged for the coming years.
Big Tech’s spending plans officially spooked Wall Street and triggered a sharp selloff in tech stocks last week that began to taper off as investors shifted focus to Tuesday’s midterm elections. Those spending plans could change after voters across the countryelected candidateswho favor moratoriums and other restrictions on data centers.
Wall Street might see the new uncertainty around the future of data center regulation as a good thing, given that tech stocks began to rise again on Tuesday. After all, there’s another issue Big Tech companies have to address. Despite enormous amounts of spending, they haven’t really made money from AI yet, and they’re continuing to double down on it anyway.
Until now, investors haven’t really blinked as Big Tech has ramped up its spending to fund the AI buildout. But more than three years in, Wall Street is starting to get antsy about the promised payoff of AI — and exactly when they might expect to see a return on investment.
It’s not that top-line revenue isn’t growing — it very much is. Amazon reported its fastest growth in five years for the quarter, Meta’s ad revenue is surging, and Google Cloud’s revenue more than doubled in a year. But as astonishing as it sounds, it might not be enough to justify the massive amounts Big Tech is spending on AI.
“Would it be more convenient if this type of acceleration and opportunity happened over 25 years and you could spread the CapEx over 25 years? Yeah, it might be more convenient. But that’s not the world we live in, and that’s not the opportunity.”
Alphabet offered the most uncomfortable example of this last week when Philipp Schindler, Google parent Alphabet’s senior vice president and chief business officer, acknowledged on the company’s earnings call that Google Cloud’s revenue growth has come at the expense of its core Search business.
“It’s worth noting that the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode,” Schindler said.
Revenue from Google’s Search ads grew 12% in the third quarter, a marked drop from the 17% growth rate the division posted for the same quarter last year.
It’s a weird paradox for Google. The strength of the company’s core business, Google Search, is what previously gave investors the confidence in the company’s aggressive spending agenda for AI. But now, Google’s new AI-enabled search engine is eating into theSearch business before the company has really figured out how to monetize AI Mode.
“To be clear, we feel very good about our trajectory here. Our ad experiments have shown promising results,” Schindler said of Google’s efforts to monetize AI Mode. He did not offer any specific examples.
Wall Street was especially unhappy with Google last week: On Thursday, Alphabet stock saw its worst one-day drop in history, sinking 13% in a single day.
The stock has started to pick back up this week, but it probably isn’t helping that the only thing Big Tech can say with certainty so far is to expect to see more spending.
Alphabet, which plans to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion in capital expenditures this year, is also planning to increase spending “significantly” in 2027, according to CFO Anat Ashkenazi.
Amazon intends to spend “meaningfully more” in 2027 than the $220 billion in capital expenditures it is planning this year, CEO Andy Jassy said on the company’s earnings call last week. He framed the spending — the largest ever in the company’s history — as a “once in a lifetime opportunity” to grow Amazon into a $1 trillion company.
“Would it be more convenient if this type of acceleration and opportunity happened over 25 years and you could spread the CapEx over 25 years? Yeah, it might be more convenient,” Jassy said. “But that’s not the world we live in, and that’s not the opportunity.”
Meta, which is expected to spend between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, didn’t disclose how much it intends to spend next year, but major financial institutions are expecting it to increase its spending from this year.
In touting the company’s rollout of Muse, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg noted that the agentic AI program will only become profitable if Meta can get its compute costs down.
Zuckerberg noted that Meta expects compute efficiency to increase “tenfold” next year, an endeavor he expects will take “significant investment.”

A Democratic sweep has changed Washington’s balance of power. But from gambling legislation to stadium subsidies, both parties have helped build the system that enriches American sports’ billionaire owners
Before a single vote was cast this election cycle, the technocrats and oligarchs who own American sports had already voted. Pro sports owners putmore than $100minto this cycle, according to Front Office Sports. But Tuesday night was a referendum not just on Donald Trump and Maga policies, but on the puppeteers who pull America’s strings. The people voted, and the owners lost.
Before anyone frames this as a rescue, a word about the rescuers. Democrats are the instrument for ending Maga, and they are also the other face of the same coin. Think Republicans are behind all of our ills? Think again. New Jersey’s governor, Phil Murphy,placed his state’s first legal sports betin 2018. Illinois governor JB Pritzkersigned sports betting into lawa year later. New York’s mobile sportsbookswent live under Governor Kathy Hochulin 2022, with the state taking 51% of the revenue. Pritzker and Hochul both won Tuesday, and all of them are Democrats. In some of the biggest betting markets in the country, the bookmakers’ most reliable partner has been a Democratic statehouse.
Having said all that, the biggest losers on Tuesday night were Republicans: Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress. That would have made plenty of sports owners disappointed, as they have a habit of backing Republicans. At least 10 sports ownersbacked Mike Rogersin Michigan, andAbdul El-Sayed beat Rogers. Dallas Cowboys ownerJerry Jonesgave$1m to Trump’s super Pacand $250,000 to a committee backing Ken Paxton, andJames Talarico beat Paxtonin Texas.
Theformer Mavericks ownerMiriam Adelson lapped everyone withat least $67mto Republican committees, in keeping withher history of big spendingaround elections. What did she get for her money? A House and Senate minority.

The NFL spent a decade teaching its fans to bet, and on 8 October itasked the US supreme courtto help protect those fans from prediction markets. Now, with the midterms shifting the balance of power in Washington, those same companies are working to rebuild ties with Democrats, who have pledged to tighten oversight of AI.

How far that gets them may depend less on image-polishing than on where the real fights are happening: in state capitols, in communities deciding whether to host data centers, and, as we’ve seen this past week, in the markets watching the AI boom.

Branch, director of federal AI governance and technology policy at Public Citizen, a nonprofit advocacy group that describes itself as nonpartisan, told me that the tech industry “realizes they have an optics problem.” He characterized moves like the Schumer hire and the rebranding as “PR washing.” He expects more of it, too, pointing to OpenAI’s partnership with the American Federation of Teachers, announced last year, as well as Anthropic’s newly launched Claude Corps and Meta’s America’s Workforce Academy.
“I would imagine more of that sort of investment in these corporate, private-public partnerships,” he said.
Meta and other tech companies reportedly began looking for ways to strengthen their ties to Democrats as Democratic gains in the midterms looked more likely.
Reached for comment about the midterm elections’ impact on Meta, a company spokesperson pointed TechCrunch to remarks that Meta President Dina Powell McCormick made this week at WSJ Tech.
“You have to work with the government that the American people elect,” McCormick had said.
“I have seen it across the board that you have to be bipartisan, and you want to be, because you want buy-in on the things that you’re trying to do.”
Alice Marwick, director of research at the tech policy nonprofit Data & Society, told me she expects Big Tech to try to pivot back toward the middle, “if not the left.
“Tech companies should be asking themselves how their products can make people’s lives better, because right now, it doesn’t seem like they are.”
If Democrats follow through on pledges to tighten oversight of AI and Big Tech, the industry could face a tougher environment.
Data center moratoriums are gaining traction, and a wave of AI regulation bills awaits drafting.

At the same event, Powell McCormick said Meta wants to show that communities welcoming its investments will see “an enormous amount of benefit,” while those that don’t want them “will of course have the right to stop them.”
Still, the next two years could bring political gridlock in Washington.

Aryan Ranjan, founder of Baraza, a political campaign management software company, told me most action will likely happen at the state level, since states have already sued tech companies and passed regulations.

“A coalition built on newer, working-class voters is likely to push Democrats to frame AI around electricity bills, data-center siting and jobs rather than abstract AI safety,” he said of what to expect at the federal level.
Last December, the Trump administration signed an executive order creating theAI Litigation Task Force, a federal group meant to challenge state AI laws.
AI companies “must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulations.” Many states have nonetheless passed their own laws, including measures on chatbots and deepfakes.
It also remains to be seen how President Trump will respond, including whether he’ll sign more AI executive orders or veto bills that could be seen as anti-AI.

In a statement to TechCrunch, a White House official said: “American leadership in super intelligence is essential for our national security, economic prosperity, and the quality of life of the American people.
President Trump is committed to ensuring America continues to lead the world in super intelligence while protecting American consumers.
As the President has said, he’s willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.”
Branch argued that Trump’s political fortunes are now tied to the AI industry.
On Wednesday, the day after the midterms, a trillion-dollar market sell-off spooked investors, some are whom are reportedly now reconsidering Anthropic’s reported trillion-dollar IPO.
“There’s a very strong likelihood that there will be an AI bubble pop, and it’ll happen on Trump’s hands,” Branch said, predicting a possible market collapse.
“Does he want to sink or swim along with the AI industry?”
For now, the rules companies face may vary by location.
“For the next two years, a company’s AI rules may depend more on where it operates rather than on anything Washington passes,” Ranjan said.

Nguồn: Mai Hân Group07/11/2026 12:01 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!Bước sang tuổi 35, nhiều chị em ngỡ ngàng nhận ra cơ thể không còn 'nghe lời' như trước. Dù nhịn ăn hay tập luyện vất vả, mỡ bụng vẫn trụ vững. Tuy nhiên, giảm cân ở độ tuổi này không hề khó nếu bạn nhận diện đúng nguyên nhân và né tránh 3 'bẫy' chuyển hóa phổ biến dưới đây để lấy lại vóc dáng thon gọn.
1. Bẫy nhịn ăn gián đoạn sai cách: Càng cắt giảm calo, mỡ bụng càng "bám chặt"
Ở ngưỡng tuổi U.35+, thói quen siết cân bằng cách cắt giảm khẩu phần ăn đột ngột hoặc bỏ bữa kéo dài thường phản tác dụng. Nguyên nhân cốt lõi nằm ở sự sụt giảm tự nhiên của tốc độ trao đổi chất cơ bản (BMR). Khi bạn nạp quá ít năng lượng, cơ thể sẽ kích hoạt chế độ "sinh tồn", chủ động hạ thấp tốc độ đốt cháy calo để tích trữ năng lượng dự trữ dưới dạng mỡ trắn; đặc biệt là vùng bụng dưới và nội tạng.
Bên cạnh đó, việc nhịn ăn nghiêm ngặt làm gia tăng hormone cortisol (hormone căng thẳng). Cortisol cao không chỉ kích thích cảm giác thèm đường và tinh bột tinh chế vào cuối ngày mà còn trực tiếp thúc đẩy quá trình tích mỡ quanh các cơ quan nội tạng.
Giải pháp các chuyên gia đưa ra để hóa giải bẫy này là chị em nên ưu tiên mật độ dinh dưỡng thay vì chỉ đếm calo. Thay vì nhịn ăn, hãy nạp đủ lượng protein chất lượng cao (thịt gà, cá, trứng, đậu hũ) để duy trì khối lượng cơ bắp. Cơ bắp chính là "lò đốt calo" hiệu quả ngay cả khi bạn đang ngủ.
Và nhớ áp dụng quy tắc đĩa ăn cân bằng là chia đĩa ăn thành 4 phần: 1/2 rau xanh giàu xơ, 1/4 protein và 1/4 tinh bột phức (khoai lang, gạo lứt, yến mạch). Sự kết hợp này giữ chỉ số đường huyết ổn định, ngăn ngừa cơn thèm ăn bộc phát.
2. Bẫy cuồng Cardio cường độ cao: Đốt cháy cơ bắp thay vì tiêu mỡ
Rất nhiều phụ nữ U.35+ tìm đến các bài tập Cardio dồn dập như chạy bộ đường dài, aerobics liên tục với mong muốn "đốt mỡ nhanh". Tuy nhiên, vận động vượt quá ngưỡng chịu đựng của cơ thể ở độ tuổi này lại mang đến hiệu quả ngược. Cardio quá đà mà thiếu bài tập kháng lực sẽ làm tiêu hao khối cơ bắp vốn đang giảm dần theo tuổi tác. Theo đó, cơ thể trở nên lỏng lẻo, thiếu độ săn chắc dù cân nặng có giảm.
Hơn nữa, tập luyện quá sức mà không phục hồi đúng cách sẽ làm trầm trọng thêm tình trạng viêm mạn tính và mất cân bằng nội tiết tố estrogen - nhân tố quyết định phân bố mỡ thừa ở phái đẹp.
Chị em muốn vượt qua "cạm bẫy" này dễ dàng nên kết hợp thông minh giữa Resistance Training và Cardio. Phụ nữ U.35+ nên dành 60-70% thời lượng tập luyện cho các bài tập kháng lực (tập với tạ, dây kháng lực hoặc tạ thân người - bodyweight). Điều này giúp kích thích tổng hợp cơ bắp và định hình đường cong vòng 2.
Đồng thời, tối ưu hóa bài tập vùng lõi (Core) là thay vì gập bụng thông thường dễ gây đau thắt lưng. Hãy ưu tiên các bài tập như Plank, Bird-Dog hay Paloff Press để siết chặt lớp cơ ngang bụng - chiếc "gen định hình tự nhiên" giúp bụng phẳng lì.
3. Bẫy coi thường giấc ngủ và sự suy giảm nội tiết tố
Đây là mắt xích thường bị bỏ qua trong hành trình giữ dáng của phụ nữ hiện đại. Sau tuổi 35, áp lực từ công việc, gia đình cùng sự suy giảm nhẹ của estrogen khiến giấc ngủ dễ bị chập chờn, ngắn và không sâu. Thức khuya hoặc thiếu ngủ mạn tính khiến hormone ghrelin (thúc đẩy thèm ăn) tăng vọt, trong khi hormone leptin (báo hiệu no) lại sụt giảm nghiêm trọng.
Kết quả là bạn luôn cảm thấy thèm đồ ngọt, thức ăn nhanh vào chiều muộn hoặc ban đêm. Thiếu ngủ cũng khiến khả năng nhạy insulin của tế bào giảm sút, dẫn đến việc chuyển hóa glucose thành mỡ thừa diễn ra nhanh hơn gấp nhiều lần.
Lúc này, các chuyên gia dinh dưỡng khuyến cáo chị em nên tập thói quen ngủ đủ giấc và đúng giờ. Đảm bảo ngủ đủ 7-8 tiếng mỗi đêm và cố gắng đi ngủ trước 23 giờ. Tắt toàn bộ thiết bị điện tử 45 phút trước khi ngủ để melatonin (hormone ngủ) được tiết ra tự nhiên.
Đồng thời, chị em nên bổ sung vi chất hỗ trợ chuyển hóa bằng cách tăng cường thực phẩm giàu Magnesium, Zinc và Omega-3 (từ cá hồi, hạt chia, quả óc chó). Nó có tác dụng làm dịu hệ thần kinh, giảm viêm mạn tính và hỗ trợ cân bằng nội tiết tố tự nhiên.
Giảm cân và duy trì vòng eo thon gọn sau tuổi 35 hoàn toàn nằm trong tầm tay nếu bạn tiếp cận bằng tư duy khoa học: lắng nghe cơ thể, nuôi dưỡng chuyển hóa thay vì ép buộc hay bóc đoản sức khỏe. Lựa chọn lối sống lành mạnh, ăn đúng - tập chuẩn - ngủ đủ chính là chìa khóa vàng giúp phái đẹp U.35+ tự tin làm chủ vóc dáng và giữ vững thần thái rạng ngời.

Quang cảnh một phiên họp Quốc hội - Ảnh: Quốc hội
Sáng nay, Quốc hội sẽ 'chốt' kế hoạch phát triển kinh tế - xã hội năm 2027
Theo chương trình kỳ họp, sáng nay 7-11, Quốc hội biểu quyết thông qua Nghị quyết về kế hoạch phát triển kinh tế - xã hội năm 2027.
Trước đó, tại báo cáo trình bày trước Quốc hội trong phiên khai mạc, Thủ tướng Lê Minh Hưng cho biết trong 45 chỉ tiêu phát triển kinh tế - xã hội của kế hoạch năm 2027 có tăng trưởng GDP phấn đấu từ 10% trở lên; tốc độ tăng CPI khoảng 4,5%; GDP bình quân đầu người đạt 6.100 USD; năng suất lao động xã hội bình quân tăng 8,6%; tỉ lệ hộ nghèo theo chuẩn nghèo đa chiều giảm 1-1,5%.
Sửa Luật Đấu thầu: Để người ngay không sợ, kẻ gian không dám, doanh nghiệp nhỏ có cơ hội
Sau đó, Quốc hội sẽ nghe trình bày tờ trình, báo cáo thẩm tra về chủ trương đầu tư 3 dự án đầu tư xây dựng đường bộ cao tốc Bảo Hà - Lai Châu, đoạn Bảo Hà - Tân Phong, cao tốc Quảng Ngãi - Kon Tum, cao tốc Mộc Châu - Sơn La - Điện Biên, địa phận tỉnh Sơn La.
Quốc hội cũng nghe tờ trình, thẩm tra dự án Nghị quyết của Quốc hội về cơ chế, chính sách đặc thù về phát triển du lịch.
Tiếp đó thảo luận ở hội trường về dự Luật Thỏa thuận quốc tế (sửa đổi).
Cuối buổi làm việc, Quốc hội thảo luận ở tổ về chủ trương đầu tư 3 dự án xây dựng đường bộ cao tốc Bảo Hà - Lai Châu, đoạn Bảo Hà - Tân Phong, cao tốc Quảng Ngãi - Kon Tum, cao tốc Mộc Châu - Sơn La - Điện Biên, địa phận tỉnh Sơn La. Cùng với đó là dự án Nghị quyết của Quốc hội về cơ chế, chính sách đặc thù về phát triển du lịch.
Căn hộ Hà Nội giá trung bình 108 triệu đồng/m², giao dịch giảm mạnh
Thị trường nhà ở Hà Nội ghi nhận thanh khoản chậm lại rõ rệt ở cả căn hộ và nhà liền thổ - Ảnh: NAM TRẦN
Theo báo cáo quý 3-2026 của Cushman & Wakefield Việt Nam, thị trường nhà ở Hà Nội ghi nhận thanh khoản chậm lại rõ rệt ở cả phân khúc căn hộ và nhà liền thổ.
Riêng phân khúc căn hộ, nguồn cung mới đạt khoảng 2.100 căn, giảm 54% so với quý trước. Lượng tiêu thụ chỉ đạt gần 1.720 căn, giảm 61% theo quý và 71% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái.
Xem tin tức mới nhất về giá vàng hôm naytại đây
Thanh khoản suy yếu trong bối cảnh giá nhà vẫn ở mức cao, nguồn cung tập trung chủ yếu ở phân khúc cao cấp, trong khi nhu cầu thị trường phần lớn đến từ người mua để ở. Một bộ phận khách hàng cũng tiếp tục chờ đợi diễn biến lãi suất và tác động của các dự án hạ tầng, quy hoạch trọng điểm.
Đáng chú ý, giá bán sơ cấp bình quân đạt khoảng 108 triệu đồng/m², giảm 12% so với quý trước. Tuy nhiên, theo Cushman & Wakefield, mức giảm này chủ yếu do tỉ trọng căn hộ hạng sang thu hẹp, trong khi nguồn cung trung cấp quay trở lại thị trường.
Thực tế, giá bán tại các dự án hiện hữu nhìn chung vẫn ổn định, thậm chí tăng phổ biến 0-2% so với quý trước.
TP.HCM giải quyết 78 kiến nghị của người dân sau kỳ họp HĐND
Ngày 6-11, UBND TP.HCM cho biết đã giải quyết 78 kiến nghị của người dân gửi đến trước và sau kỳ họp thứ ba HĐND TP.HCM khóa XI.
Theo báo cáo của UBND TP.HCM, qua các đợt tiếp xúc trước và sau kỳ họp, HĐND TP.HCM đã chuyển 628 lượt ý kiến, kiến nghị đến UBND TP.HCM xem xét, giải quyết.
Bí thư Trần Lưu Quang mong đại biểu HĐND TP.HCM đeo đuổi đến cùng giải quyết kiến nghị của dân
Các kiến nghị tập trung vào những vấn đề người dân quan tâm như dự án chậm tiến độ, hạ tầng giao thông, nhà ở xã hội, giấy phép xây dựng; chế độ chính sách, an sinh xã hội, thủ tục hành chính, đất đai, bồi thường và tái định cư.
Trong đó, nhóm quản lý dự án, hạ tầng giao thông, nhà ở xã hội và giấy phép xây dựng chiếm khoảng 47%; chế độ chính sách, cải cách thủ tục hành chính và an sinh xã hội chiếm khoảng 30%; đất đai, bồi thường, tái định cư và môi trường chiếm khoảng 20%.
UBND TP.HCM đã yêu cầu các sở, ngành và địa phương rà soát, trả lời từng nội dung. Văn phòng UBND TP.HCM cũng có 10 văn bản đề nghị bổ sung, hoàn thiện câu trả lời, bảo đảm kiến nghị của người dân được xem xét đầy đủ.
TP.HCM lập kế hoạch hành động về đa dạng sinh học đến năm 2030
Đường Rừng Sác, tuyến huyết mạch đi Cần Giờ hiện nay - Ảnh: CHÂU TUẤN
UBND TP.HCM vừa ban hành kế hoạch hành động về đa dạng sinh học trên thành phố đến năm 2030, tầm nhìn đến năm 2050.
Theo kế hoạch, đến năm 2030, thành phố đặt mục tiêu gia tăng diện tích hệ sinh thái tự nhiên được bảo vệ, phục hồi, bảo đảm tính toàn vẹn và kết nối sinh thái. Thành phố sẽ thành lập mới Khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên Cần Giờ giai đoạn 2026-2030; xây dựng hồ sơ đề cử rừng ngập mặn Cần Giờ trở thành khu Ramsar - vùng đất ngập nước có tầm quan trọng quốc tế.
Đồng thời, thành phố phấn đấu duy trì ổn định tỉ lệ che phủ rừng ở mức 11%, đồng thời tăng cường bảo tồn các loài động, thực vật hoang dã, nhất là các loài nguy cấp, quý, hiếm và loài di cư.
Kế hoạch cũng đặt mục tiêu tăng diện tích cây xanh, không gian xanh và mặt nước đô thị, phục hồi các hệ sinh thái tự nhiên, khuyến khích các giải pháp dựa vào thiên nhiên.

U.35+ giảm cân không khó, cần tránh 3 bẫy này là có ngay vòng eo con kiến

Nguồn: Mai Hân Group07/11/2026 12:01 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!Bước sang tuổi 35, nhiều chị em ngỡ ngàng nhận ra cơ thể không còn 'nghe lời' như trước.
Dù nhịn ăn hay tập luyện vất vả, mỡ bụng vẫn trụ vững.
Tuy nhiên, giảm cân ở độ tuổi này không hề khó nếu bạn nhận diện đúng nguyên nhân và né tránh 3 'bẫy' chuyển hóa phổ biến dưới đây để lấy lại vóc dáng thon gọn.
Bẫy nhịn ăn gián đoạn sai cách: Càng cắt giảm calo, mỡ bụng càng "bám chặt"
Ở ngưỡng tuổi U.35+, thói quen siết cân bằng cách cắt giảm khẩu phần ăn đột ngột hoặc bỏ bữa kéo dài thường phản tác dụng.
Nguyên nhân cốt lõi nằm ở sự sụt giảm tự nhiên của tốc độ trao đổi chất cơ bản (BMR).
Khi bạn nạp quá ít năng lượng, cơ thể sẽ kích hoạt chế độ "sinh tồn", chủ động hạ thấp tốc độ đốt cháy calo để tích trữ năng lượng dự trữ dưới dạng mỡ trắn; đặc biệt là vùng bụng dưới và nội tạng.
Bên cạnh đó, việc nhịn ăn nghiêm ngặt làm gia tăng hormone cortisol (hormone căng thẳng).
Cortisol cao không chỉ kích thích cảm giác thèm đường và tinh bột tinh chế vào cuối ngày mà còn trực tiếp thúc đẩy quá trình tích mỡ quanh các cơ quan nội tạng.
Giải pháp các chuyên gia đưa ra để hóa giải bẫy này là chị em nên ưu tiên mật độ dinh dưỡng thay vì chỉ đếm calo.
Thay vì nhịn ăn, hãy nạp đủ lượng protein chất lượng cao (thịt gà, cá, trứng, đậu hũ) để duy trì khối lượng cơ bắp.
Cơ bắp chính là "lò đốt calo" hiệu quả ngay cả khi bạn đang ngủ.
Và nhớ áp dụng quy tắc đĩa ăn cân bằng là chia đĩa ăn thành 4 phần: 1/2 rau xanh giàu xơ, 1/4 protein và 1/4 tinh bột phức (khoai lang, gạo lứt, yến mạch).
Sự kết hợp này giữ chỉ số đường huyết ổn định, ngăn ngừa cơn thèm ăn bộc phát.
Bẫy cuồng Cardio cường độ cao: Đốt cháy cơ bắp thay vì tiêu mỡ
Rất nhiều phụ nữ U.35+ tìm đến các bài tập Cardio dồn dập như chạy bộ đường dài, aerobics liên tục với mong muốn "đốt mỡ nhanh".
Tuy nhiên, vận động vượt quá ngưỡng chịu đựng của cơ thể ở độ tuổi này lại mang đến hiệu quả ngược.
Cardio quá đà mà thiếu bài tập kháng lực sẽ làm tiêu hao khối cơ bắp vốn đang giảm dần theo tuổi tác.
Theo đó, cơ thể trở nên lỏng lẻo, thiếu độ săn chắc dù cân nặng có giảm.
Hơn nữa, tập luyện quá sức mà không phục hồi đúng cách sẽ làm trầm trọng thêm tình trạng viêm mạn tính và mất cân bằng nội tiết tố estrogen - nhân tố quyết định phân bố mỡ thừa ở phái đẹp.
Chị em muốn vượt qua "cạm bẫy" này dễ dàng nên kết hợp thông minh giữa Resistance Training và Cardio.
Phụ nữ U.35+ nên dành 60-70% thời lượng tập luyện cho các bài tập kháng lực (tập với tạ, dây kháng lực hoặc tạ thân người - bodyweight).
Điều này giúp kích thích tổng hợp cơ bắp và định hình đường cong vòng 2.
Đồng thời, tối ưu hóa bài tập vùng lõi (Core) là thay vì gập bụng thông thường dễ gây đau thắt lưng.
Hãy ưu tiên các bài tập như Plank, Bird-Dog hay Paloff Press để siết chặt lớp cơ ngang bụng - chiếc "gen định hình tự nhiên" giúp bụng phẳng lì.
Bẫy coi thường giấc ngủ và sự suy giảm nội tiết tố
Đây là mắt xích thường bị bỏ qua trong hành trình giữ dáng của phụ nữ hiện đại.
Sau tuổi 35, áp lực từ công việc, gia đình cùng sự suy giảm nhẹ của estrogen khiến giấc ngủ dễ bị chập chờn, ngắn và không sâu.
Thức khuya hoặc thiếu ngủ mạn tính khiến hormone ghrelin (thúc đẩy thèm ăn) tăng vọt, trong khi hormone leptin (báo hiệu no) lại sụt giảm nghiêm trọng.
Kết quả là bạn luôn cảm thấy thèm đồ ngọt, thức ăn nhanh vào chiều muộn hoặc ban đêm.
Thiếu ngủ cũng khiến khả năng nhạy insulin của tế bào giảm sút, dẫn đến việc chuyển hóa glucose thành mỡ thừa diễn ra nhanh hơn gấp nhiều lần.
Lúc này, các chuyên gia dinh dưỡng khuyến cáo chị em nên tập thói quen ngủ đủ giấc và đúng giờ.
Đảm bảo ngủ đủ 7-8 tiếng mỗi đêm và cố gắng đi ngủ trước 23 giờ.
Tắt toàn bộ thiết bị điện tử 45 phút trước khi ngủ để melatonin (hormone ngủ) được tiết ra tự nhiên.
Đồng thời, chị em nên bổ sung vi chất hỗ trợ chuyển hóa bằng cách tăng cường thực phẩm giàu Magnesium, Zinc và Omega-3 (từ cá hồi, hạt chia, quả óc chó).
Nó có tác dụng làm dịu hệ thần kinh, giảm viêm mạn tính và hỗ trợ cân bằng nội tiết tố tự nhiên.
Giảm cân và duy trì vòng eo thon gọn sau tuổi 35 hoàn toàn nằm trong tầm tay nếu bạn tiếp cận bằng tư duy khoa học: lắng nghe cơ thể, nuôi dưỡng chuyển hóa thay vì ép buộc hay bóc đoản sức khỏe.

Europe's crisis of discontent: Student and cost-of-living protests spread across EU

12:12 minSharePlay (12:12 min)From the showReading time1 min
A growing wave of discontent is sweeping across Europe. What began in France as student protests over deteriorating school conditions, teacher shortages and an education system under pressure has quickly grown into something much bigger: a groundswell of discontent over the rising cost of living, unaffordable housing and struggling public services.
Theunresthas spread beyondFrance, with demonstrations inBelgium,Germany,Italy,SpainandPortugal. While many marches have remained peaceful, some have descended into violence, withclashes, looting and destruction. The response from authorities has also come under scrutiny for excessive use of force and mass arrests.
This discontent comes against a backdrop of mounting economic pressure. France, the EU's second-largest economy, is facing sluggish growth and risingpublic debt, projected to reach 120 percent ofGDPby 2027. Meanwhile,inflationacross both theEuropean Unionand theeurozonehit 3.8 percent in September, up from 2.1 percent in 2024.
IsEuropefacing a wider crisis of public discontent and could this be a tipping point for governments already struggling to maintain public trust?

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckx2:
French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living - BBC News
The head of France's CGT labour union, Sophie Binet (C), said the wave of protests and strikes had reached a new level
More than 600,000 protesters have taken part in rallies and marches across France, according to France's interior ministry, with five unions joining a day of action demanding more money for wages and public services.
The left-wing CGT union put the number of people taking part in Thursday's mobilisation at 1.57 million and hailed the figure as "a level unmatched" since 2023, citing big protests in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and Lille.
As darkness fell in Paris, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he would convene a "social conference" with unions and employers next Monday.
The wave of protests began in September over poor conditions and resources atlycées(high schools), before spreading to universities, workers and a revived "yellow-vest" movement against high prices.
The unions had vowed to take the co-ordinated move against the government "to the next level", and CGT chief Sophie Binet had said their message was that "the only thing that will bring this mobilisation to a halt is responding to our demands".
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had earlier deployed 70,000 police, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.
Some unrest was reported in several cities.
A car was set alight near the Gallieni bridge over the Rhône river in Lyon, as hundreds of activists from the radical left-wing "black bloc" clashed with police.
Clashes were also reported in the north-western city of Rennes, where the local prefect said a "hostile group of masked individuals" had gathered in front of the main union march. Tear gas was used to clear a square in the south-western city of Bordeaux and a teenager was hurt in a stabbing involving a student at a high-school blockade in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.
But the trouble was not on the scale seen during the last big day of protests, on Saturday 17 October, when more than 2,000 stores were looted and historic buildings set on fire.
The provisional numbers reported on Thursday were higher than on 17 October, considered the biggest day of rallies until now when the interior ministry said 550,000 people had turned out and the unions counted 800,000.
Earlier on Thursday the leader of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, said she would be happy if the protests matched that earlier level.
A car was set alight during a protest in the centre of Lyon
A coalition of unions across the public and private sector had urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, orSmic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour.
Sophie Binet told reporters at the start of a march in central Paris that protesters had "just reached a new level in their mobilisation" and were demanding immediate answers.
An estimated 9.89% of civil servants were taking part in the strikes, according to government figures.
Disruption was reported in schools, hospitals and public transport, and the Eiffel Tower and some exhibition rooms at the Louvre museum in Paris had to close.
Workers were also asked to halt production at oil refineries and France was expected to import more electricity than it produced on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants.
Image source,Philippe LOPEZ / AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,
Disruption was already reported at schools on Thursday morning
The head of the CFDT complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase. "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month," Marylise Léon explained.
The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopularParcoursupuniversity admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028.
The prime minister said early on Thursday evening that Monday's "social conference" with unions and employers would seek to "provide answers to questions surrounding purchasing power and wages".
However, the government by its own admission has little room to manoeuvre, as it looks to make tens of billions of euros in savings, in a bid to cut the budget deficit to 5% of GDP.
The education ministry said that 16% of teachers had gone on strike on Thursday, and the unions said disruption had affected more than one in four lycées, which cater for 15-18 year-olds, as well as the vast majority of universities.
"Now it's not only about [investing in] public services in education and higher education, it's about all of the public services in France," the vice-president of the Unef student union, Alice De Brito, told the BBC.
Meanwhile, a revivedgilets jaunes(yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too.
'Everyone hates the police' – what France's school protests reveal about a divided nation
France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
Thursday's march was eventually allowed in central Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon.
Instead, the march followed another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation.
The interior minister had earlier spoken of three potential risks on Thursday, from radical left "black blocs" groups and looting to wildcat marches without union authorisation.

Updated:5 November 2026 - 14:45 GMT+1
Hundreds of thousands joined a fourth nationwide day of protests across France. Police used tear gas outside a Paris school, while major demonstrations disrupted Marseille and Nantes.
France was gripped by anationwide day of strikes and demonstrationson Thursday 5 November, as trade unions mobilised workers, students and other protesters to demandhigher wages, tax justice and better public services.
By 1 pm, the Interior Ministry had counted270,000 demonstrators across 180 marchesoutside Paris, while the CGT reported more than 250,000 participants in 73 cities. Around70,000 police officers and gendarmes were deployed nationwide, 81 secondary schools were blockaded and15.81% of teachers joined the strike.
In Marseille, thousands marched from Les Réformés towards Place Castellane, waving union flags and lighting flares as police monitored the procession.Seventeen metro stations were closed.
In Nantes,around 30,000 people took to the streetsaccording to organisers, compared with a police estimate of 24,000, after unions secured permission to march through the city centre.
In Paris, tensions erupted outside Lycée Honoré-de-Balzac in the 17th arrondissement, wherepolice used tear gas to disperse studentsprotesting a lack of resources for education.
Footage showed a firework exploding above the crowd, cardboard burning in a bin outside the school gates and officers moving in to clear the area. Police alsodismantled another student blockadeon Rue de Rivoli. The capital'smain union march set off from Place de la République at 2 pm, following a route imposed by authorities towards Place de la Nation.
The mobilisation markedanother major test of the autumn protest movement, bringing together workers, students and public-sector employees amidgrowing demands for improved pay and working conditions.

A growing wave of discontent is sweeping across Europe.

What began in France as student protests over deteriorating school conditions, teacher shortages and an education system under pressure has quickly grown into something much bigger: a groundswell of discontent over the rising cost of living, unaffordable housing and struggling public services.
While many marches have remained peaceful, some have descended into violence, withclashes, looting and destruction.
The response from authorities has also come under scrutiny for excessive use of force and mass arrests.
This discontent comes against a backdrop of mounting economic pressure.
France, the EU's second-largest economy, is facing sluggish growth and risingpublic debt, projected to reach 120 percent ofGDPby 2027.
Meanwhile,inflationacross both theEuropean Unionand theeurozonehit 3.8 percent in September, up from 2.1 percent in 2024.
IsEuropefacing a wider crisis of public discontent and could this be a tipping point for governments already struggling to maintain public trust?

French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living - BBC News
The head of France's CGT labour union, Sophie Binet (C), said the wave of protests and strikes had reached a new level

More than 600,000 protesters have taken part in rallies and marches across France, according to France's interior ministry, with five unions joining a day of action demanding more money for wages and public services.

The left-wing CGT union put the number of people taking part in Thursday's mobilisation at 1.57 million and hailed the figure as "a level unmatched" since 2023, citing big protests in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and Lille.
As darkness fell in Paris, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he would convene a "social conference" with unions and employers next Monday.
The wave of protests began in September over poor conditions and resources atlycées(high schools), before spreading to universities, workers and a revived "yellow-vest" movement against high prices.

The unions had vowed to take the co-ordinated move against the government "to the next level", and CGT chief Sophie Binet had said their message was that "the only thing that will bring this mobilisation to a halt is responding to our demands".
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had earlier deployed 70,000 police, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.
A car was set alight near the Gallieni bridge over the Rhône river in Lyon, as hundreds of activists from the radical left-wing "black bloc" clashed with police.
Clashes were also reported in the north-western city of Rennes, where the local prefect said a "hostile group of masked individuals" had gathered in front of the main union march.

Tear gas was used to clear a square in the south-western city of Bordeaux and a teenager was hurt in a stabbing involving a student at a high-school blockade in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.
But the trouble was not on the scale seen during the last big day of protests, on Saturday 17 October, when more than 2,000 stores were looted and historic buildings set on fire.

The provisional numbers reported on Thursday were higher than on 17 October, considered the biggest day of rallies until now when the interior ministry said 550,000 people had turned out and the unions counted 800,000.
Earlier on Thursday the leader of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, said she would be happy if the protests matched that earlier level.
A car was set alight during a protest in the centre of Lyon
A coalition of unions across the public and private sector had urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government.
In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, orSmic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour.
Sophie Binet told reporters at the start of a march in central Paris that protesters had "just reached a new level in their mobilisation" and were demanding immediate answers.
An estimated 9.89% of civil servants were taking part in the strikes, according to government figures.
Disruption was reported in schools, hospitals and public transport, and the Eiffel Tower and some exhibition rooms at the Louvre museum in Paris had to close.
Workers were also asked to halt production at oil refineries and France was expected to import more electricity than it produced on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants.

1:53'Shameful chapter': King Charles stops short of slavery apology in Commonwealth speech – video
King Charles addresses summit as demands for slavery apology grow
Speaking in Antigua, the king did not give explicit support for reparations but said he wanted to ‘address past wrongs’
King Charles has said that deepening his understanding of the horrors of slavery has made him more determined to address the wrongs of the past, asCaribbeanleaders and campaigners intensified demands for an apology and reparations from Britain.
“We cannot change the actions of those who came before us,” Charles told leaders at the opening of theCommonwealth summitin Antigua and Barbuda on Tuesday. “We can, however, learn from the past.
“The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth,” he said. “That shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow.”
Charles said the more he had furthered his understanding “through listening, learning and looking”, the more committed he had become to building modern partnerships capable of addressing past wrongs.
But the king stopped short of an apology or explicit support for reparations, instead pointing to education, employment, intra-Commonwealth trade and climate resilience as ways of tackling continuing hardship and disadvantage.
10:21Will the UK finally pay slavery reparations? – The Latest
“For, as any sailor navigating the seas knows, we cannot command the winds, least of all where the winds of yesterday have delivered us, but we can choose how we set our sail,” he said.
Though speaking as head of the Commonwealth, and this speech would have been drafted by Charles personally along with his advisers, palace aides have indicated there would be “no surprises” in it for the UK government.
Andy Burnham refused to be drawn on whether the UK might offer further financial contributions to the Commonwealth stopping short of direct reparations.
View image in fullscreenAndy Burnham walks to meet members of the waiting media on the sidelines of the summit at the American University of Antigua in Osbourn.Photograph: Kin Cheung/Reuters
The UK prime minister told reporters: “I’ve been very clear that we do not support reparations, and I made that quite abundantly clear in the piece that I wrote in advance of coming here.
“But it’s not the case that we don’t support countries in the Commonwealth around development and helping them with debt issues that they’ve got, green finance. That’s what we’ve done under all governments, and in my view, we should continue to do as part of being a Commonwealth.”
Pressed on whether this could mean additional financial contributions that would weigh on the taxpayer, Burnham said: “Well, you’re getting ahead. What we need to have is that meaningful dialogue where we take time to listen, and let’s be clear: the Commonwealth is an important part of our trade too.
“It’s a two-way arrangement. You know, trade is up between the UK and the rest of the Commonwealth in the last year quite significantly, actually. So you need to see it in that way as well. It benefits Britain to be here, listening to people, building that new partnership, and that’s good for growth in Britain.”
Reparations are not formally on the agenda of the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (Chogm), where trade, climate resilience and finance, sustainable debt, democracy and opportunities for young people were among the stated priorities of the 56-member bloc.
But sustained campaigning by Caribbean governments and agrowing international reparations movementhave propelled the issue to the centre of political debate surrounding the gathering.
View image in fullscreenKing Charles III speaks with students during the Commonwealth Youth Forum at the University of West Indies in St John’s, Antigua.Photograph: Chris Jackson/PA
Opening the summit in St John’s, the capital of Antigua and Barbuda, the country’s prime minister, Gaston Browne, said “fairness” required an “honest engagement with our shared history” and called for meaningful and respectful dialogue on reparatory justice and the enduring consequences of slavery and colonialism.
Burnham had said he wasopen to Britain apologisingfor slavery, with officials holding talks with national leaders in Antigua about what that could entail.
He has also proposed discussions on debt resets for smaller Commonwealth nations and announced £40m ($54m) for critical infrastructure in the Caribbean over the next three years.
But Caribbean leaders have stressed that dialogue must extend beyond an apology. Philip J Pierre, the chair of theCaribbean Community (Caricom), described an apology as an “essential first step” but said an “apology without repair is incomplete”.
He said any structured dialogue must allow consideration of the entirety ofCaricom’s 10-point reparations plan, including public health, education, cultural restitution, psychological rehabilitation, debt cancellation and monetary compensation.
Britain’sroyal family benefited from the trade, but Charles is politically neutral and is not expected to offer an apology. A palace spokesperson said it would “not be appropriate” for the king to announce a change in government policy.
According to the AFP news agency, Burnham discussed slavery with the Barbados prime minister, Mia Mottley, during a meeting on Monday, one of several bilateral meetings the prime minister is expected to have at the summit.
View image in fullscreenBurnham is said to have discussed the impact of slavery with Mia Mottley during talks on Monday.Photograph: Kin Cheung/PA
They discussed how Britain was “offering a structured dialogue for communities impacted by the transatlantic slave trade”, including the “next steps”, Downing Street said.
Outside the heavily secured summit venue, protesters gathered with placards declaring: “We know what you did and we can see you,” and “You say appalling atrocity, yet you refuse to apologise.”
One protester, Lenworth Johnson, said that if the king’s constitutional position prevented him from apologising, the British government should authorise him to do so. “We feel an apology is necessary,” he said.
